Public contributors participated in a national survey to identify and rank priorities for preconception health research in Scotland and attended a multi-stakeholder workshop to refine and finalise research themes and questions. The workshop included members of the public alongside researchers, healthcare professionals, third sector representatives, and policy stakeholders, ensuring that priorities reflected lived experience as well as professional perspectives. Public input directly informed the identification of research priorities, the interpretation of findings, and the development of future research directions (See the GRIPP2 short form checklist in the supplementary files).

items.title: Accessing and Navigating Gender-Affirming Hormone Therapy and Perspectives on Inclusive Pharmacy Care Among Transgender and Gender Diverse People: A Qualitative Study.
items.authors: McCann J, Wilcock S, Dominy I, Davison K, Sharman S, Robinson-Barella A.
items.abstract:
Introduction

Transgender and gender diverse (TGD) people continue to experience inequities in access to gender-affirming care, including stigmatisation, delayed treatment and non-inclusive healthcare encounters. Community pharmacies may represent an accessible setting to support inclusive and affirming care; however, lived experiences of engaging with community pharmacy services in the context of gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) remain underexplored, particularly among younger people who represent the greatest proportion of the TGD community. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences of accessing, navigating and receiving GAHT, alongside participants' perspectives on barriers and facilitators to accessing inclusive and affirming care within community pharmacy.

Methods

Semi-structured interviews were conducted between October and November 2025. Interviews explored participant experiences of accessing GAHT and perspectives on inclusive and affirming pharmacy practice. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. NVivo (Version 15) facilitated data management, and the COREQ and CCRF checklists informed reporting. Ethical approval was obtained from the Newcastle University Research Ethics Committee (reference: 66105/2023).

Results

Ten participants, representing a range of gender identities, were interviewed. Three overarching themes were developed: (1) reflecting on the challenges of navigating gender-affirming hormone therapy; (2) exploring the impact of healthcare barriers upon an individual and (3) accessing and receiving inclusive and affirming pharmacy care. Participants viewed community pharmacies as accessible and supportive environments for affirming care when underpinned by respectful communication, visible inclusivity, appropriate staff training and partnership working with TGD communities.

Conclusion

In this study, TGD individuals described significant structural and interpersonal barriers when accessing GAHT in the United Kingdom, negatively influencing trust, wellbeing and engagement with healthcare services. Community pharmacies may represent an underutilised, yet important, setting for inclusive and gender-affirming support. Embedding gender-affirming training and co-designed approaches within pharmacy services may strengthen accessibility, trust and equity in care for TGD communities.

Lived experience or public contribution

A person with lived experience from the TGD community (ID) acted as a co-author and patient champion in this study; they supported the design and conduct of the research, advised on inclusive and non-stigmatising approaches and supported preparation of the manuscript, contributing a lived-experience perspective throughout.

items.title: Implementation and Performance of a Clinical Debriefing Programme in a Paediatric Emergency Department: A Descriptive Qualitative Review.
items.authors: Reeves KL, Batty A, Plummer K.
items.abstract:
Objective

Clinical debriefing should be standard practice in healthcare, but in most emergency departments implementation lags behind evidence. This post-implementation evaluation examined the performance of a clinical debriefing programme in a tertiary care paediatric emergency department, exploring implementation, key enablers and barriers to use.

Methods

This qualitative descriptive, post-implementation study used semi-structured interviews, with deductive analysis guided by a context-mechanism-outcome framework.

Results

Twenty-one multidisciplinary staff were interviewed. Debriefing became embedded in routine practice through organisational endorsement, structured facilitation and inclusive participation. Participants reported improved clinical reasoning, emotional regulation, psychological safety and interprofessional relationships. Debriefing strengthened support for junior staff, enhanced relational co-ordination across disciplines, facilitated more timely quality and safety actions and built nursing capacity to lead debriefs. Time was the principal barrier, but reframing debriefing as an integral component of clinical care enabled its routine delivery.

Conclusions

Clinical debriefing was embedded in routine practice through interactions between organisational context and implementation mechanisms, with successful implementation relying on both the intervention and the conditions enabling it. Benefits for clinical practice, staff well-being, teamwork, enhanced support for the junior workforce and timely quality improvement initiatives were described. This study advances current understanding and provides direction for teams seeking to implement or optimise debriefing within their own departments.

items.title: Time, Trust and Participation: A Nationwide Quantitative Study of Person-Centred Care in Forensic Mental Health Settings.
items.authors: Vidaurrázaga Aras V, Wolf A, Nilsson T, Alexiou E, Olausson S.
items.abstract: Person-centred care emphasises the uniqueness of individuals through partnerships, the co-creation of care plans and coordinated health care. Its implementation in forensic mental health services is challenged by legal coercion and restrictive practices. Person-centred principles are embedded in legislation; however, national data on patients' perspectives on person-centred care are lacking. This study aimed to map person-centred care as perceived by patients and to identify areas for improvement. A nationwide survey included 329 patients across 13 forensic psychiatric hospitals in Sweden using the Generic Person-Centred Care Questionnaire supplemented with contextual background questions. The median Generic Person-Centred Care Questionnaire score was 70 (range 19-95). Length of stay was associated with perceived person-centred care; patients hospitalised for 2-5 years reported higher total scores than those hospitalised for more than 10 years, although the pairwise difference did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Trust in staff differed by length of stay, with patients hospitalised for > 10 years reporting significantly lower trust than those hospitalised for 0-1 and 2-5 years. Communicative safety showed a similar pattern, although pairwise differences were not significant after correction. No significant differences in total scores were found by gender, age, ethnicity, diagnosis, or hospital type. Overall, patients reported positive experiences of respect and emotional support. Among those who reported having a written care plan, involvement in and understanding of the plan were rated positively, whereas broader involvement in decision-making, use of patients' own resources and relatives' participation received lower ratings, indicating areas for further improvement in person-centred practice.

items.title: Astrocytic EAAT-2 Upregulation Supports Neuro-Axonal Homeostasis in Chronic Inflammatory CNS Lesions.
items.authors: Reukauf L, Margineanu A, Muinjonov B, Chen J, Cui Y, Rosiewicz K, Radbruch H, Munro I, Alisch M, Siffrin V.
items.abstract: Neuronal loss in multiple sclerosis (MS) is a key factor in the progression of disability. Axonal degeneration within MS lesions is central to progressive MS pathology, yet its mechanisms are not fully understood. Excess extracellular l-glutamate (GLUT) is neurotoxic due to overstimulation of GLUT receptors. Excitotoxicity, driven by GLUT, is a suspected contributor to several central nervous system (CNS) diseases. Astrocytic glutamate transporters EAAT-1 and EAAT-2 play crucial roles in managing extracellular GLUT, yet their role in chronic MS remains underexplored. Using the animal model experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) and advanced microscopy in live anesthetized mice, we examined GLUT-mediated neurotoxicity and protective mechanisms in chronic CNS lesions. By employing genetically encoded fluorescent biosensors, we visualized extracellular GLUT levels and axonal Ca<sup>2+</sup> dynamics within the live mouse brain during EAE. In acute EAE, extracellular GLUT levels were high, while in chronic lesions, normalized GLUT levels together with sustained EAAT-2 upregulation were consistent with a protective astrocytic response. EAAT-2 inhibition in chronic lesions led to higher intra-axonal Ca<sup>2+</sup> levels and morphological changes consistent with neuroaxonal injury, indicating that EAAT-2 upregulation may counter excitotoxicity and support neuroprotection. Post-mortem MS brain tissue analysis provided complementary evidence, showing elevated EAAT-1 and EAAT-2 expression in chronic MS lesions with expression patterns varying according to lesion type and cellularity. This study highlights astrocytic mechanisms that may contribute to neuroaxonal protection in MS tissue and suggests targeting GLUT transporters as a promising strategy to limit neurodegeneration in progressive MS.

items.title: Working Right Ways: Investigating Health Practitioners' Perspectives of Foot Health and Needs for Providing Good Foot Care With and for First Nations Peoples.
items.authors: Gerrard J, Godwin Badimaya Yamatji S, Whiteley Wiradjuri K, Charles Kaurna J, Chuter V.
items.abstract:
Background

History of invasion, ongoing colonisation, and systemic racism excluding First Nations Peoples from healthcare are root causes of health inequalities including disparities in foot health outcomes. Sources of inquiry into current practice, learning, and experience, which may shape reform of providing good foot care with and for First Nations Peoples in the land now known as Australia are health practitioners working in the space. This work seeks to explore foot care service delivery by investigating First Nations and non-Indigenous health practitioners' perspectives regarding providing foot care with and for First Nations Peoples.

Methods

Ways of working are documented in previous work; 'Working right ways in foot health with and for First Nations Peoples: research method guided and governed by First Nations ways of knowing, being, and doing in cross-sectional qualitative study design'. First Nations and non-Indigenous health practitioners provided perspectives with culturally responsive semi-structured interviews guiding talking with consenting participants. Coding utilised constant comparison techniques to explore patterns across the dataset. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

Results

Two talking points engaged health practitioners' perspectives of providing foot care with and for First Nations Peoples: (1) What does foot health mean to you as a First Nations or non-Indigenous health practitioner? (2) What are needs for providing good foot care with and for First Nations Peoples? Within responses, themes emerged of mobility and participation, overall health and wellbeing, clinical and biomedical perspective, and advocacy being related to the meaning of foot health. The requirements of cultural safety, workforce, and holistic care were perceived as needed for provision of good foot care with and for First Nations Peoples.

Conclusion

Participants described a meaning of foot health that is relational to physical and spiritual constructs, and central to reclamation of, and continuation of, First Nations cultures; amidst a project of ongoing colonisation. Needs for good foot care provision with and for First Nations Peoples included a workforce continually learning and unlearning to develop cultural capabilities to work with and for, and support, First Nations foot health. This study provides distinct and real first-hand accounts from health practitioners working in the space which the podiatry profession must listen to and receive direction and learning from.

items.title: An Explainable Self-Supervised Temporal Transformer for Participant-Level Classification of Depressive Symptoms From Resting-State EEG.
items.authors: Ramaiah P, Nomani I, Asfour HI, Baig MR, Yuldashev M, Sapaev I, Bani Younes ZB, Sharma S, Manchanda M, Khasawneh MAS, Jabir MS.
items.abstract:
Background

Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising non-invasive modality for investigating depressive symptoms; however, conventional deep-learning methods often require large labeled datasets and provide limited interpretability. We developed an Explainable Self-Supervised Temporal Transformer Network for participant-level classification of BDI-defined elevated depressive symptoms from resting-state EEG.

Methods

The framework employed masked temporal modeling for self-supervised pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning. Model performance was evaluated using repeated nested participant-wise cross-validation and compared with conventional machine-learning and deep-learning baselines. Explainability was investigated through transformer attention maps and SHAP-based channel attribution.

Results

The proposed model achieved a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.73-0.90), a precision-recall AUC of 0.69, balanced accuracy of 0.75, sensitivity of 0.72, and specificity of 0.78. The positive predictive value was 0.57, indicating a substantial false-positive burden in the evaluated cohort. The proposed model showed the highest point-estimate ROC-AUC among the evaluated baselines, with a 0.07 improvement over EEGNet; however, the overlapping uncertainty intervals and the small elevated-symptom cohort warrant cautious interpretation of comparative superiority. Performance decreased from an ROC-AUC of 0.82 in Run 1 to 0.78 in Run 2 and to 0.72-0.73 under cross-condition transfer, supporting interpretation of these analyses as internal reproducibility and condition-shift assessments rather than independent external validation. Removing self-supervised pretraining reduced the ROC-AUC to 0.74. Explainability analyses identified distributed temporally relevant intervals and frontal-midline to centro-parietal channel contributions, with attribution interpreted as model-relevance evidence rather than causal biomarker evidence.

Conclusion

Overall, the findings provide preliminary internal evidence that self-supervised temporal representation learning can support participant-level classification of BDI-defined elevated depressive symptoms from resting-state EEG under the evaluated experimental conditions. The findings do not establish clinical diagnostic validity, screening readiness, or independent external generalizability.

items.title: Machine Learning in Causal Effect Estimation and Causal Evaluation of ML-Enabled Interventions in Nursing-Related Research: A Scoping Review.
items.authors: Kosmidis D, Vlachopoulos G, Nashwan AJ, de Carvalho RLR, Araujo BS, Armeni D, Sertaridou E, Koutsouki S.
items.abstract: Machine learning (ML) informs nursing practice, but prediction cannot establish intervention or workflow effects. Aim To map ML use within causal effect estimation and causal evaluations of ML-enabled interventions in nursing and midwifery. Eight electronic sources were searched for reports published January 2015-June 2026, followed by backward citation searching. Eligibility required a causal estimand, corresponding identification strategy, substantive ML role, and nursing or midwifery relevance. Two reviewers independently screened records and full texts. Fifteen studies (17 reports) were included. Five addressed acute deterioration or sepsis; others covered care prioritization, falls, post-discharge care, and nurse- or midwife-led services. Five used ML within causal effect estimation to examine longitudinal and spillover effects, treatment-effect heterogeneity, and targeting strategies. Ten evaluated ML-enabled interventions or workflows; reported favorable effects on mortality, care escalation, message-review time, and nursing processes, while several controlled estimates were null or imprecise. Evidence remains small and methodologically uneven. Future studies should align estimands, identification strategies, analytic methods, and workflows and evaluate model-plus-workflow effects on nursing processes and patient outcomes.

items.title: Concordance of Microbiological and Histopathological Examination of Bone Biopsies in Diagnosing Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis, a Systematic Review.
items.authors: Kadiri L, Maher A, Bridgen A.
items.abstract:
Background

Diabetic foot osteomyelitis (DFO) is a serious complication of diabetic foot ulcers and is associated with increased risk of amputation, morbidity, and mortality. Bone biopsy remains the most definitive diagnostic modality, yet controversy persists over its diagnostic utility This study reviews the diagnostic concordance of histopathology and microbiology in bone biopsy specimens from patients with DFO and examines the clinical implications of the findings.

Methods

A systematic review was conducted using PubMed, Medline, CINHAL, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. Studies included adult patients with DFO in whom bone biopsy specimens underwent both histopathological and microbiological analysis. Five core studies met the eligibility criteria. Data on study design, setting, population, diagnostic methods, concordance rates, and outcomes were extracted and synthesized utilising a quantitative narrative synthesis.

Results

Across the five studies (n = 308 patients), histopathology and microbiology showed modest concordance, with mean rates of concordant positive results of 43.4% and common discordant findings. Histopathology demonstrated higher specificity, while microbiology had higher sensitivity, ranging from 70% to 83.9% but greater susceptibility to contamination. Positive histopathology was more strongly associated with the need for revision surgery or extended antibiotic therapy.

Discussion

Histopathology appears to offer superior diagnostic specificity, whereas microbiology provides valuable information for antimicrobial management. Frequent discordance underscores the importance of interpreting results in a clinical context. Further robust, prospective studies are needed to clarify the optimal diagnostic approach and standardise definitions.

items.title: MADE: leveraging informative missingness and temporal evaluation for electronic health record-based deterioration prediction in general wards.
items.authors: Mun Y, Ahn JH, Lee CY, Ahn B, Huh JW, Chung KS.
items.abstract:
Objective

Electronic health record (EHR) time series are irregularly sampled and frequently incomplete, with missingness potentially carrying clinically informative signals. We developed Masked-Attention-based timestamp-wise Data Embedding (MADE), a missingness-aware model for continuous prediction of deterioration in general wards, and evaluated it across heterogeneous hospitals.

Materials and methods

Observed variables were tokenized into feature-specific embeddings and processed by a masked-attention Transformer, followed by bi-LSTM temporal aggregation for risk prediction. MADE was evaluated for major adverse event (MAE) and sepsis in 1 internal (SVH) and 2 external cohorts (AMC, HUMC) against conventional and deep learning baselines. Ablation studies compared no imputation with last observation carried forward (LOCF) and multiple imputations by chained equations (MICE). Discriminative performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Clinical utility and reliability were assessed using decision curve analysis, Brier score, and expected calibration error (ECE).

Results

MADE achieved strong discrimination for MAE (AUROC 0.966/0.902/0.825 for SVH/AMC/HUMC) and sepsis (AUROC 0.934/0.874/0.776). The no-imputation configuration generally outperformed LOCF and MICE, particularly for MAE and for sepsis AUPRC, supporting preservation of informative missingness. Decision curves showed favorable net benefit for MAE and competitive benefit for sepsis. Calibration indicated modest underestimation at higher risks, suggesting site-specific recalibration.

Discussion

MADE mitigates limitations of fixed grid and imputation-dependent EHR modeling by jointly leveraging observed values and missingness patterns under heterogeneous sampling.

Conclusion

MADE supports scalable observation-aligned risk monitoring, particularly for MAE, while sepsis prediction may require site-specific recalibration or feature-set adaptation under cross-institution domain shifts.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-based diagnostic decision support for primary care of older adults using collective intelligence and imitation learning.
items.authors: Streiffer CD, Press MJ, Bishop NS, Schmid BE, Sliwa A, Vyas AL, Ungar LH, Peifer M, Weissman GE.
items.abstract:
Objective

Older adults face disproportionate risk of diagnostic errors in primary care, yet effective diagnostic decision support systems (DDSSs) remain lacking. Existing artificial intelligence (AI)-based DDSSs rely on gold-standard labels infeasible to obtain, have narrow diagnostic scope, and fail to reflect real-world uncertainty. We developed and validated a deep learning DDSS using imitation learning and collective clinician intelligence to generate diagnostic and order recommendations.

Materials and methods

We trained a multi-label neural network on structured and unstructured electronic health record data from primary care encounters of adults ≥65 years old to imitate clinician decisions. Models were evaluated using discrimination, calibration, threshold-based, and composite metrics on a temporally held-out test set. Clinical validity was assessed using a randomized, blinded equivalence study comparing model-generated recommendations with observed clinician decisions.

Results

The study included 707 598 primary care encounters, generating recommendations across 669 diagnoses and 1000 orders. The general model demonstrated excellent performance (micro c-statistic 0.995 [95% CI 0.995-0.996], macro c-statistic 0.896 [0.888-0.897], micro F1-score 0.904 [0.903-0.905], macro F1-score 0.384 [0.381-0.385], integrated calibration index (ICI) 0.0025 [0.0024-0.0026]). Order prediction was lower (micro c-statistic 0.812 [0.811-0.814], macro c-statistic 0.786 [0.777-0.786], micro F1-score 0.305 [0.303-0.307], macro F1-score 0.0286 [0.0277-0.0294], ICI 0.0145 [0.0141-0.0150]). In clinician-validation, diagnostic disagreements were statistically equivalent between model recommendations and observed practice while order disagreements were not.

Conclusion

Imitation learning and collective clinician intelligence provide a feasible framework for generating diagnostic and ordering recommendations that reflect real-world practice without expert-adjudicated training labels. Randomized, blinded clinician evaluation pragmatically establishes preliminary clinical validity beyond traditional retrospective metrics.

items.title: velotest: statistical assessment of RNA velocity embeddings reveals quality differences for reliable trajectory visualizations.
items.authors: Bischoff S, Poličar PG, Mukherjee S, Macke JH, Claassen M, Schröder C.
items.abstract: Contemporary single-cell RNA-sequencing studies typically use RNA velocity analyses to investigate cellular dynamics. Commonly, RNA velocities are assessed with two-dimensional projections. Although it is well established that nonlinear embeddings of gene expression data cannot comprehensively preserve the structure of the original high-dimensional data across scales, there is no tool that systematically assesses and quantifies the faithfulness of velocity embeddings. This situation potentially leads to misleading velocity visualizations and putative cell state transitions. To this end, we introduce velotest, a cell-level statistical test that quantifies the faithfulness of a velocity embedding with respect to its high-dimensional counterpart. Applying velotest across multiple datasets and embedding methods, we find strong differences in the embedding qualities between embedding methods, datasets, and regions in individual datasets. velotest thus provides an essential validation step and enables researchers to select a suitable visualization of high-dimensional velocities, ensuring that hypotheses drawn from velocity projections are grounded in accurately represented dynamics.

items.title: Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction Reveals Distinct Phenotypic Clusters Among Immediately Placed Dental Implants: A UMAP Analysis of 5-Year Outcomes.
items.authors: Cheng YC, Puisys A, Gallucci GO, Vindasiute-Narbute E, Nasseri A, Zvirblis T, Pala K.
items.abstract: This study applied uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP), a nonlinear dimensionality reduction algorithm, to high-dimensional data from immediately placed and immediately loaded dental implants in the anterior maxilla to identify distinct phenotypic clusters and explore whether preoperative characteristics are associated with 5-year esthetic outcomes in this exploratory proof-of-concept study. Twenty-two patients who received immediately placed and immediately loaded implants in the anterior maxilla were analyzed. A total of 103 clinical, radiographic, and patient-reported parameters were collected across preoperative, baseline, 1-year, and 5-year time points. UMAP and principal component analysis (PCA) were used to generate two-dimensional representations of the data. K-means clustering was applied to the UMAP embeddings, and Mann-Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction were used for inter-cluster comparisons. UMAP fitted on all 103 parameters separated the 22 implants into four clearly defined clusters. Clusters differed significantly in 5-year white esthetic score (WES; P < .001 after Bonferroni correction), as well as in pink esthetic score (PES), orofacial esthetic scale (OES), soft tissue height, and buccal bone thickness (all P < .05). PCA did not generate separable clusters. UMAP fitted on 24 preoperative parameters alone separated implants into three clusters that differed significantly in tooth location (P < .001) and showed divergent 5-year outcomes in OES and periodontal probing depth (PPD). UMAP identified clinically meaningful phenotypic clusters among immediately placed and immediately loaded implants that were not apparent using conventional linear methods. Clusters characterized by favorable initial bone conditions achieved superior long-term esthetic outcomes. Preoperative UMAP clustering was associated with 5-year outcomes in this exploratory proof-of-concept analysis; validation in independent cohorts is needed.

items.title: CogD-ML: Cognitive determinants of social commerce purchase intention in Bangladesh using machine learning and explainable AI.
items.authors: Barua S, Rahman R, Azad AKA, Momen S.
items.abstract: Cognitive factors are associated with online purchase intentions in developing economies, and the linear models conventionally used to study them can miss non-linear patterns. We report an applied integration of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) with machine learning and explainable AI (XAI) to predict social media-driven e-commerce purchase intentions in Bangladesh. Survey data from 352 young, student-dominated consumers captured attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and purchase behavior on validated Likert scale items. After reliability-based labeling and feature selection, we ran an ablation across seven classical classifiers and one multilayer perceptron, with stratified five-fold cross-validation, threshold sensitivity analysis, and a cross-domain check. With all TPB constructs included, support vector machines and AdaBoost reached 92% accuracy on the held-out test set, and cross-validated mean accuracy ranged from 0.84 to 0.88 for every model except the decision tree. These figures should be read against a positive-class prevalence of 82.1%, which inflates accuracy and F1 relative to imbalance-robust measures. Transfer to an independent North Indian sample was weak, with SVM MCC falling from 0.522 to 0.315 and AUROC from 0.923 to 0.775. In SHAP analyses, the four items the model relied on most were PBC1 (motivation from frequent advertising), SN3 (approval when many others buy through social media), ATTD4 (past purchase), and SN1 (family influence). Bivariate correlations and pathway-level regression with Benjamini-Hochberg correction are interpreted as associations, not causal effects, and Brier score and log loss are reported alongside SHAP and LIME to show whether predicted probabilities are calibrated. These findings are exploratory and specific to the sampled population; given the convenience sample, the class imbalance, and the weak transfer, they are not evidence of robust generalization or of readiness for deployment.

items.title: Online unsupervised industrial anomaly detection with adaptive resonance patch prototype memory and multi-level views.
items.authors: Zhu Y, Li P, Zhang Q, Jin G.
items.abstract: Unsupervised industrial anomaly detection is widely used because defective samples are scarce while normal data are abundant. Many recent methods follow a feature-embedding pipeline that models patch-level deep features, but they often (i) introduce cross-layer interference when multi-level features are fused and (ii) risk losing fine-grained information when reference features are aggressively reduced. This paper proposes ART-IAD, an online patch-based framework that treats multi-level CNN features as independent views and models each view with an incremental Fuzzy Adaptive Resonance Theory (Fuzzy ART) prototype memory. For each ART prototype, sufficient statistics, including the mean and covariance, are maintained, and Mahalanobis-based anomaly scores are computed, enabling anomaly detection and localization without storing all patch embeddings. On MVTec AD, ART-IAD achieves an average image-level AUROC of 99.4% and pixel-level AUROC of 98.2%, slightly outperforming the strong baseline PatchCore by +0.3% in image-level AUROC and +0.1% in pixel-level AUROC. These results indicate that ART-based online prototype modeling and multi-view separation can provide accurate detection and localization with a compact reference memory.

items.title: NeuroSim: a clinically informed multi-disorder EEG simulator with personalized pattern injection and AI-driven neurological modeling
items.authors: Bunterngchit C, Aslam S, Sattar A, Rasool A, Wang Y.
items.abstract: Deep learning for electroencephalography (EEG) based neurodiagnostics is constrained  by the limited availability of labeled clinical recordings. Datasets covering Alzheimer’s  disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), schizophrenia (SCZ), epilepsy (EPI), and  frontotemporal dementia (FTD) are scarce, demographically narrow, and heterogeneous  across acquisition sites, while privacy requirements restrict data sharing. Existing EEG  simulators typically address a single disorder or trade biological interpretability for  statistical fidelity. This study presents NeuroSim, a simulation framework that  generates synthetic multichannel EEG with user-controlled injection of disease-specific  patterns across five disorders and multiple severity levels. A physiologically motivated  baseline generator produces band-limited rhythms, event-related potentials, artifacts,  and hierarchical subject-level and trial-level variability. Disease patterns are introduced  through region-specific and severity-specific spectral modulation that encodes  established biomarkers, including posterior alpha suppression in AD, motor beta  enhancement in PD, and spike-wave discharges in EPI. An interactive interface exposes  montage, sampling rate, duration, artifacts, stimuli, affected regions, and severity, and  exports signals with reproducible metadata. The simulated signals reproduced the  expected biomarker directionality under spectral, topographic, and multivariate  statistical analysis. A convolutional-attention classifier trained on simulated data  reached 95.3 to 96.8 percent hold-out accuracy, and post hoc explainability analyses  produced class-separable embeddings with attributions concentrated on  pathophysiologically expected electrodes. Application of the analysis pipeline to  recordings from the Temple University Hospital EEG Corpus confirmed compatibility  with heterogeneous clinical data. In subject-level augmentation experiments on real  clinical EEG, supplementing real training data with NeuroSim samples increased  classification accuracy from 91.6 to 94.5 percent for AD versus healthy controls and  from 90.9 to 94.0 percent for PD versus healthy controls, exceeding the improvement  obtained with conventional signal-level augmentation. NeuroSim is released as open-source software to support augmentation, benchmarking, and explainable artificial  intelligence in neurological diagnostics.

items.title: BrainRoute integrates machine learning prediction with community-driven verification of blood-brain barrier permeability
items.authors: Shirolkar SA, Bueh LT, Cerere LW, Ahmed NE, Some G, Awe OI.
items.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a highly selective barrier that restricts the entry of many therapeutic agents into the brain. The lack of efficient methods for BBB permeability research and data management remains a significant challenge for central nervous system drug-development pipelines. Although BBB permeability data are available from multiple open sources, few platforms integrate these datasets with molecular exploration, predictive tools, and a structured process for community-supported data verification. Here, we present BrainRoute, an open platform for BBB molecular data collection, exploration, prediction, and community-supported verification. BrainRoute provides searchable and filterable molecular records, physicochemical and structural information, source-linked data, single-molecule and batch prediction, and a structured workflow through which users can submit additional evidence for review. The prediction tool model-development cohort contained 7,888 unique molecules, including 5,424 BBB+ and 2,464 BBB- molecules. Six machine-learning classifiers were evaluated using PaDEL descriptors, Morgan fingerprints, frozen ChemBERTa embeddings, and combined feature representations. The three selected models were integrated into the platform as a probability-averaged ensemble. The primary five-fold scaffold-grouped analysis achieved a best mean balanced accuracy of 0.783 ± 0.026. On an independent external set containing 410 non-overlapping molecules, the deployed ensemble achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.659 (95% CI 0.600 - 0.712) and an AUPRC of 0.670 (95% CI 0.583 - 0.752). BrainRoute serves as a platform for exploring BBB-related molecular data and computational predictions while supporting the continued growth and verification of the underlying dataset. BrainRoute is freely accessible online (https://github.com/omicscodeathon/brainroutedb).

items.title: The ITE-Transformer: A pre-trained foundation model for predicting individualized treatment effects from electronic health records
items.authors: Arceri C, Angelis E, Heesen P, Melnychuk V, Bendszus M, Bauer S, Feuerriegel S.
items.abstract: Transformer-based foundation models have shown strong potential for modeling longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), yet existing models focus primarily on risk prediction rather than treatment effect estimation, which limits evidence generation. Here, we introduce the ITE-Transformer, a transformer-based framework that combines self-supervised representation learning from longitudinal patient trajectories with doubly robust causal machine learning for predicting individualized treatment effects (ITEs). As a result, our ITE-Transformer allows to study counterfactual questions of how an individual patient's outcome may differ under alternative treatment strategies. The ITE-Transformer learns temporally contextualized representations of patients' diagnosis and medication histories and subsequently uses these representations to predict treatment assignment, treatment-specific outcome risks, and patient-specific ITEs. The ITE-Transformer is trained using structured EHR data from ~350,000 participants in the All of Us Research Program and evaluated in two clinically different comparative-effectiveness tasks: (i) GLP-1 receptor agonists versus DPP-4 inhibitors among patients with type 2 diabetes, with major adverse cardiovascular events as the outcome, and (ii) immunotherapy versus chemotherapy in a pan-cancer cohort, with all-cause mortality as the outcome. Across both applications, the ITE-Transformer improves the discrimination and calibration of treatment assignment and outcome models compared with existing tabular machine learning approaches and an otherwise identical transformer trained without self-supervised pre-training. The ITE-Transformer further identifies substantial heterogeneity in predicted ITEs and yields interpretable patterns of treatment response associated with patients' diagnoses, medication histories, and comorbidities. Together, our work demonstrates how clinical foundation models can be developed for analyzing heterogeneity in treatment effects and thus support real-world evidence generation.

items.title: Examining HiTOP Through Naturalistic Symptom Descriptions in Anonymous Online Mental Health Forums: A Mixed-Methods Study Protocol
items.authors: Ferizaj D.
items.abstract:
AbstractBackground: The Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP) organises covarying symptoms and maladaptive traits into transdiagnostic dimensions to address limitations of categorical diagnosis. Naturalistic symptom descriptions may complement structured assessments.

Objective:

This protocol describes a reproducible mixed-methods workflow to derive symptom indicators from forum posts and examine their organisation relative to HiTOP. Methods and analysis: The target sample is 80,000 public Reddit posts. After local de-identification, a large language model (LLM) will extract symptom labels and supporting paraphrases. Two human experts will independently review outputs for up to 250 posts. Three embedding models will flag potentially equivalent symptom labels for local LLM assessment. Two experts will qualitatively review the most frequent canonical symptom labels (at least 1,000) and develop a codebook of symptom categories, continuing until a prespecified saturation criterion is met. An LLM will assign canonical symptom labels to these categories, producing binary post-level indicators. Multiverse-inspired structural analyses will compare network, component, factor, and clustering representations across discovery, internal tuning, and holdout partitions. Evaluation will assess interpretability, stability, and agreement with expert mapping to HiTOP. Supplementary analyses will include agent-assisted exploration, codebook application to DepressionEmo and the Reddit Mental Health Dataset, and pooled integrative analysis that may include additional comparable corpora.

Discussion:

The study will examine whether symptom co-expression within posts forms interpretable patterns corresponding to HiTOP.Ethics: The Ethics Committee of Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin approved the study (EA2/274/25). The study was preregistered on 8 May 2026 (German Clinical Trials Register, DRKS00040244).

items.title: Bayesian Physics-Informed Neural Networks Embedded in Finite Element Analysis: A Probabilistic Digital Twin for Reliability-Based Design of FDM Polymer Components
items.authors: Zahmatkeshan MH, Biglari FR, Dariani BM.
items.abstract: Digital twin technology presents revolutionary possibilities for additive manufacturing, but current applications are limited to deterministic forecasting that does not capture manufacturing uncertainties. This study introduces a probabilistic digital twin system that uses machine learning and finite element analysis in two synergistic innovations. First, a Bayesian physics-informed neural network predicts material properties as Abaqus input with quantified uncertainty by embedding Euler-Bernoulli beam theory within a Monte Carlo dropout architecture. Second, the trained network's deterministic forward pass is embedded directly within an Abaqus user material subroutine, enabling material property evaluation at each integration point for a given sampled modulus value, while the probabilistic Monte Carlo dropout sampling is performed externally prior to each finite element run. This framework was constructed based on experimental data of sixty 3D-printed polylactic acid specimen groups subjected to three-point bending in accordance with ISO 178, with validation against ten independent configurations with raster angles ranging from zero to ninety degrees. Monte Carlo finite element analysis propagated material property uncertainty through the simulation, yielding stress predictions with calibrated confidence intervals. The framework achieved a coefficient of determination of 0.9935 with a mean absolute percentage error of 1.85%, and 95% confidence intervals contained experimental values in all ten validation cases, consistent with (though not sufficient to precisely confirm, given the limited sample size) well-calibrated uncertainty estimates. Reliability analysis revealed that the 60° raster angle (8.0% CV) and 90°/80% reduced infill configuration (9.0% CV) exhibit more than double the prediction uncertainty compared to the optimal 0° orientation (3.8% CV), informing correspondingly adjusted safety factors. The computational overhead of the embedded neural network added only 15% to simulation time while eliminating the need for external property pre-computation. This work demonstrates a full probabilistic digital twin framework for additively manufactured polymer components under flexural loading, enabling reliability-based design choices that are challenging to implement under deterministic methods. The framework provides a foundation for advancing additive manufacturing toward structural applications that require a quantified performance margin.

items.title: AOPedex: AOP-based endocrine disruption extrapolation as white-box mechanism maps for zero-data species
items.authors: Gao Y, Zhang Y, Chen G, Luo N, Ji Y, Gu Y.
items.abstract: Endocrine disruption evidence is concentrated in a handful of model species, leaving risk assessment for ‘zero-data species’ unresolved; scarce toxicity records and biologically untraceable black-box extrapolation constrain machine learning. We present AOPedex, a knowledge-driven white-box framework embedding ToxCast in vitro activity, receptor binding-pocket conservation and traceable close-relative evidence in a deterministic AOP event-network propagation skeleton, so that mechanistic maps share one source for prediction, attribution and audit. Across 5,387 compounds and 756 vertebrate species, 94.4% of species are high-confidence or predictable, including 123 IUCN threatened species. Under identical protocols, EBM matches TabPFN in macro out-of-fold ROC-AUC on seven general-toxicity endpoints (0.810 versus 0.812) and outperforms it on data-sparse Morphology (0.698 versus 0.661). Controlled AON polarity randomisation barely changes ROC-AUC but disrupts mechanistic ordering, showing that predictive performance does not imply mechanistic validity. AOPedex audits receptor inputs, AON propagation, model readouts and literature evidence, yielding applicability-domain-conditioned mechanistic predictions, candidate screening regions and testable molecular entry points and event chains. Experimental feedback revises priors for iterative computation–experiment calibration. AOPedex aims to turn observations of model species into knowledge of many more so that toxicological knowledge serves biodiversity.

items.title: Discourse coherence in first-episode psychosis and depression: shared referential alterations and links to cortical hierarchy
items.authors: ÇOKAL D, Villalba M, vogeley k, Böke A, He R, von Heusinger K, Hinzen W, Kambeitz J.
items.abstract: Disrupted discourse coherence is documented in psychosis, but whether depression shows similar alterations, and how these relate to cortical hierarchical organization, remains unclear. This is the first study to examine conceptual and referential dimensions of coherence and their associations with cortical hierarchy across first-episode psychosis and depression. We analysed spontaneous speech from 85 German speakers (29 controls, 28 with first-episode psychosis, 28 with first-episode depression), of whom 80 underwent resting-state fMRI. Using large-model embeddings, automated coreference resolution, and graph-theoretical measures, we quantified conceptual relations (i.e., how ideas are linked) and referential relations (i.e., how entities are introduced and maintained), and related them to gradient dispersion between networks and within the semantic-associative network. Both clinical groups showed reduced referential continuity, and less small-world organization of conceptual content than controls, whereas differences in local semantic similarity depended on diagnosis and language model. Negative symptom severity was associated with altered conceptual and referential relations. Between-network gradient dispersion did not differ between groups. However, after controlling for diagnosis, individual variation in gradient organization was associated with distinct conceptual and referential relations. Visual-default mode network dispersion was associated with conceptual network organization, while somatomotor-default mode network dispersion was associated with local conceptual and referential coherence. Dispersion within the semantic-associative network was linked with topic reorganization. These findings identify reduced referential continuity as a shared, automatically measurable speech alteration across early psychosis and depression, linked to negative symptoms and cortical hierarchy, and support developing scalable speech-based markers for transdiagnostic assessment and differential diagnosis.

items.title: Lynch syndrome and other hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes: insights from establishing an oncogenetic tertiary centre in Romania
items.authors: Munteanu CV, Perva IT, Simina IE, Nagy ED, Barna R, Geana VO, Nacov F, Negru S, Chirita-Emandi A, Trifa AP.
items.abstract: Lynch syndrome (LS) is among the most common hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes, caused by germline variants in the mismatch repair genes MLH1 , MSH2 , MSH6 and PMS2 , or by EPCAM 3' deletions. Its clinical utility is well established, yet Romanian data remain scarce and germline testing is poorly covered by public healthcare. We retrospectively reviewed 481 consecutive patients referred to a large oncology centre in Timișoara, Romania (2023–2025) for suspected LS or another hereditary cancer syndrome, assessing germline testing yield. Each patient was assessed against the NCCN Colorectal criteria (v1.2023) and their 2026 update (Colorectal, Endometrial and Gastric, v1.2026). A subset of urothelial tract carcinomas was further characterised by whole exome sequencing, MMR immunohistochemistry and FGFR3 hotspot analysis. The cohort comprised 481 patients (56.3% female), with gastrointestinal (46.2%), gynaecological (23.0%) and reno-urinary (20.3%) malignancies accounting for nearly 90% of cases. Germline testing was performed in 153 patients (31.8%) and identified pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in 37 (24.2%): 21 in LS genes and 16 in other predisposition genes, predominantly BRCA1 . Retrospective application of NCCN 2026 core criteria increased eligibility from 183 (38.0%) to 209 patients (43.5%). Category 2B (colorectal and gastric cancer ≥ 50 years) added 109 further eligible patients but no additional Lynch cases, instead capturing three non-Lynch variants ( BRCA1 , ATM , biallelic MUTYH ). Urothelial carcinomas represented 3.9% of the cohort, with two uncertain germline BRCA2 variants identified, consistent with emerging evidence of a broader BRCA2 -associated cancer spectrum. Category 2B thus widened eligibility without improving LS detection, though it captured hereditary variants that would otherwise have been missed. Urothelial cancers were strikingly underrepresented despite ranking third among LS-associated malignancies. Germline testing carries clear diagnostic value in this setting, but referral and access remain uneven, an argument for broader reimbursement and for embedding oncogenetic evaluation into routine Romanian oncology care.

items.title: Implementing risk stratification in UK glaucoma services: a qualitative study of barriers and facilitators
items.authors: Jones L, Sii F, Shah P.
items.abstract: Background / Objectives: Rising demand for glaucoma services has intensified the need for effective prioritisation of patients according to clinical risk. This study explored clinicians’ perspectives on glaucoma risk stratification and identified barriers and facilitators to implementing stratification systems within UK glaucoma services. Subjects / Methods: A qualitative study using semi-structured interviews was conducted with ophthalmologists, allied health professionals, and service managers involved in glaucoma care. Participants were recruited using purposive sampling. The interview topic guide was informed by the Theoretical Domains Framework, and transcripts were analysed using inductive thematic analysis. Results: Eighteen participants from nine institutions were interviewed. Four major themes were identified: (1) reflections on glaucoma management and the role of risk stratification; (2) barriers to implementation; (3) facilitators supporting adoption; and (4) perceived benefits of risk stratification. Key barriers included the clinical heterogeneity of glaucoma, limitations in electronic medical record systems, time constraints, and variation in organisational support. Facilitators included educational initiatives, embedding stratification within electronic patient records, leadership endorsement, and demonstrating measurable service benefits. Participants highlighted potential advantages including improved prioritisation of high-risk patients, more efficient allocation of clinical resources, and potential for enhanced patient safety. Conclusions : Systematic risk stratification is perceived as valuable for improving glaucoma service delivery; however, successful implementation requires coordinated technological, organisational and behavioural change. Embedding stratification within digital systems, supported by education, leadership and robust evidence, will be critical to achieving sustainable adoption within routine clinical practice.

items.title: MedCapVQA: A Two-Stage Explainable Framework for Medical Visual Question Answering
items.authors: Perera N, Nummenmaa J, Stefanidis K.
items.abstract: Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA) aims to answer natural language questions about clinical images and has significant potential for diagnostic support, medical education, and improved access to expert interpretation. Most Med-VQA systems fuse image features and question embeddings directly, a mapping that is hard to learn from the few thousand question--answer pairs that medical benchmarks provide and that is usually compensated for with large-scale domain pre-training. We propose \modelname{}, a two-stage, caption-driven framework that describes the image first and answers the question second. A MedGemma captioner, adapted with parameter-efficient fine-tuning on ROCOv2, converts each medical image into a clinically meaningful caption; a BioBERT-based reasoner with dedicated caption and question encoders and question-to-caption cross-attention then predicts the answer from text alone. We evaluate \modelname{} on the closed-ended questions of the VQA-Med 2019 benchmark, training on the official training set (3,200 medical images, 12,792 question--answer pairs) and evaluating on the official validation set (500 images, 2,000 question--answer pairs), against six baselines that represent the main prior design families: a convolutional--recurrent fusion model, BioBERT and Med3D domain-adapted variants, a self-attention fusion network, a Vision Transformer model with cross-attention, and an end-to-end fine-tuned vision-language model. All models are trained under the same protocol and across training-set proportions from 5\% to 100\%, with each data-size result averaged over ten random training subsets. \modelname{} achieves the highest validation accuracy on both tasks: 81.9\% on binary (yes/no) questions, 11.6 percentage points above the strongest baseline, and 73.9\% on 71-category multiclass questions, 5.4 points above the fine-tuned vision-language model and 13.5 points above the Vision Transformer model. The vision-language model attains a higher multiclass training accuracy but lower validation accuracy compared to \modelname{} and none of the baseline models are strong on both tasks. The \modelname{} reasoner trains on a single GPU in $\sim$5 hours. These results show that converting medical images into textual captions before reasoning is an effective and resource-efficient alternative to direct multimodal fusion, and they highlight the value of intermediate semantic representations for the design of next-generation Med-VQA systems.

items.title: Toward Unified Efficient Sequence Modeling from Kernelized Attention to State Space Transformers via Spectral Operator Theory
items.authors: Xu J.
items.abstract: Creating efficient models of long sequences has become a primary challenge within many modern applications of AI such as: natural language processing (NLP), scientific computing, large-scale time series forecasting, and multimodal learning. The Transformer architecture has shown state-of-the-art performance across a wide variety of sequence modelling tasks, but the computational and memory complexity due to its reliance on an attention-based mechanism poses significant scalability limitations for long-context applications. In anticipation of overcoming the limitations of the existing models, this research proposes the Unified Spectral Operator (USO-Former) framework for modelling sequences. The proposed architecture consists of five principle components: (1) A Multi-Scale Embedding Layer for computing the sequence representations at different resolutions to learn a hierarchy of sequence representations; (2) A Kernelized Spectral Attention Module for efficiently modelling the contextual interactions of the input sequence elements; (3) A Spectral State Space Memory Block for ensuring long-range dependency preservation; (4) An Adaptive Fusion Mechanism to effectively integrate the contextual and memory-based representations of the input sequence; and (5) An Adaptive Multi-Objective Spectral Swarm Optimization (AMOSSO) strategy for simultaneously optimizing predictive accuracy, memory usage, computational efficiency, and training stability. We conducted extensive experiments on the Long Range Arena (LRA), PG-19, and WikiText-103 benchmark datasets and compared the predictive performance of the USO-Former to that of the conventional Transformer, Performer, Longformer, Mamba, and RWKV architectures. The USO-Former produced the highest predictive accuracy across all test datasets, achieving an accuracy of 89.7% on LRA, 92.1% on PG-19, and 93.4% on WikiText-103, exceeding the accuracy of the conventional Transformer baseline models by 6.5%, 6.1%, and 5.6%, respectively. Additionally, the proposed framework produced superior resource efficiency; requiring only 4.60GB of RAM as compared to the 12.40GB required by the Transformer, while also reducing the total computational workload to 96GFLOPs and achieving the fastest inference speed of 71ms of all evaluated architectures.

items.title: Integrating social work into interdisciplinary pain management: advancing equitable care for women with chronic pain.
items.authors: Moorehead LA.
items.abstract: Chronic pain is one of the most common causes of disability in the United States and disproportionately affects women, particularly those experiencing gender, racial, and socioeconomic inequities. Biomedical paradigms continue to dominate pain care, neglecting the social and structural determinants that shape women's pain experiences. This integrative review examines the potential role of social workers in advancing equitable, trauma-informed, and person-centered pain management for women within interdisciplinary health care systems. Peer-reviewed literature across pain medicine, behavioral health, and social work was synthesized to identify theoretical frameworks, practice competencies, and equity considerations that position social workers to address inequities in pain assessment and treatment. Evidence from interdisciplinary pain management broadly suggests improvements in patient satisfaction, functional outcomes, and health equity, particularly among women from marginalized populations; direct evidence isolating social work's specific contribution to these outcomes remains limited. Core competencies include biopsychosocial assessment, care coordination, advocacy, and culturally responsive education. Embedding social workers in interdisciplinary pain teams and institutionalizing trauma-informed and equity-driven standards may reduce disparities and may support a redefinition of healing as the restoration of agency, dignity, and justice for women living with chronic pain.

items.title: Addressing Disparities in Hypertension Control: The Potential Role of New Drugs and Devices in 2026 and Beyond.
items.authors: Odo CC, Reddy T, Ogunniyi MO, Ferdinand KC, Ilonze OJ.
items.abstract:
Purpose of review

Hypertension is the leading modifiable cardiovascular risk factor in the United States, with racially/ethnically diverse populations experiencing a disproportionate burden, associated with social, structural, and potentially biological determinants. This review examines how recently approved and investigational pharmacologic therapies and device-based interventions may advance hypertension control in 2026 and beyond, with deliberate attention to the strength and applicability of the available evidence in racially/ ethnically diverse populations.

Recent findings

Aldosterone synthesis and mineralocorticoid receptor signaling represent important advances beyond the present guidelines for resistant hypertension and cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk reduction. For instance, baxdrostat, a recently approved aldosterone synthase inhibitor (ASI), has demonstrated clinically meaningful blood pressure reductions. In addition, lorundrostat, an investigational ASI, provides a model for racially representative trial design through the intentional enrollment of Black and Hispanic/Latino participants and consistent efficacy across racial subgroups. In contrast, pivotal finerenone trials demonstrated improved cardiac and renal outcomes but included limited representation of Black adults. Additional approved therapies include an agent targeting the endothelin pathway, aprocitentan, and device-based interventions via renal denervation therapy, although their effectiveness in diverse populations remains unknown. Therapies targeting natriuretic peptide signaling remain investigational but could potentially expand the therapeutic landscape. Advances in antihypertensive therapy offer new opportunities to improve blood pressure control and reduce cardiovascular risk beyond the 2025 American Heart Association (AHA) and American College of Cardiology (ACC) AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline-directed approach. Ensuring equitable benefit from these innovations requires that therapeutic innovation be coupled with deliberate efforts to ensure equitable delivery and benefit across populations.

items.title: Financial distress, clinic attendance concerns and transport-support requests for long-acting injectable HIV options among people living with HIV and clients recruited through PrEP services in Uganda: a cross- sectional study
items.authors: Olet SC, Muluga WU, Nakabaale M, Muluga F, Musiho R, Among F, Nait C, Mulyowa A, Ongom S, Stecher CD, Kiwanuka SN, Musoki D.
items.abstract: Background Long-acting injectable HIV products reduce daily medication demands but require scheduled clinic visits. We examined associations of financial distress with anticipated clinic attendance concern and requests for transport support among people living with HIV and clients recruited through pre-exposure prophylaxis services in Uganda. Methods In this exploratory analysis, we used a cross-sectional survey of 232 participants, comprising 116 people living with HIV and 116 clients recruited through PrEP services. Concern about strict clinic attendance requirements was defined as concerned or highly concerned on a four-level item. Financial distress meant difficulties meeting basic needs sometimes, often or always during the previous three months. Modified Poisson models estimated prevalence ratios adjusted for service group, age group and sex. Secondary analyses examined food worry, meal skipping, transport mode, concern thresholds and service-support preferences. Results Overall, 109/232 participants (47.0%) reported attendance concern. Concern was more frequent with financial distress than without it (64.9% versus 41.1%, adjusted prevalence ratio 1.37, 95% confidence interval 1.02–1.84). Food worry showed an uncertain association (1.33, 0.99–1.80), while meal skipping showed no clear association (1.14, 0.83–1.56). Threshold-specific adjusted odds ratios for financial distress were 3.17 (1.40–7.17) for any response above not concerned, 2.12 (1.08–4.19) for concerned or highly concerned, and 1.04 (0.45–2.40) for highly concerned. Fourteen of 17 participants who walked reported concern (82.4%, adjusted prevalence ratio 1.58, 1.15–2.17). Participants with financial distress more often requested transport support (36.8% versus 8.0%, adjusted prevalence ratio 3.86, 1.91–7.81). Within-group estimates were larger among clients recruited through PrEP services (6.66) than among people living with HIV (1.94), with an interaction p-value of 0.09. Conclusions Financial distress was moderately associated with anticipated attendance concern and strongly associated with requesting transport support. Food-related measures provided weaker evidence. Injectable HIV service planning should assess financial and travel constraints alongside product preferences and evaluate practical support for scheduled visits.

items.title: ADSMoE: A mixture-of-experts-based transformer autoencoder for discovering multimodal Alzheimer's disease subtypes
items.authors: Meng W, Pan J, Yin M, Zhuang P, Gong K, Lin M, Xu J, Burns M, Wu Y, Yin R.
items.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits substantial biological and clinical heterogeneity, posing critical challenges for advancing precision medicine. Existing data-driven approaches often rely on modality-specific clustering or predefined biomarker trajectories, limiting their ability to discover disease subtypes from incomplete, heterogeneous real-world data. In this study, we introduce ADSMoE, a mixture-of-experts (MoE)-based multimodal representation learning framework that jointly identifies AD subtypes as latent disease signatures while accommodating incomplete modality combinations. ADSMoE integrates a Fleximodal MoE encoder that accommodates arbitrary combinations of available modalities with a novel subtype-specific MoE decoder to capture complementary disease characteristics through expert specialization. Using data from 5,422 participants across three independent cohorts, we trained ADSMoE on the ADNI cohort and externally validated the identified subtypes in NACC and UKB without model retraining. The proposed ADSMoE identified four AD subtypes with distinct neuroimaging patterns, genetic and proteomic associations, and clinical characteristics. Benchmarking analyses demonstrated robust subtype discovery and strong biological and clinical relevance, while external validation revealed consistent subtype-associated characteristics across independent cohorts. ADSMoE advances AD subtyping by uncovering biologically and clinically meaningful AD heterogeneity from incomplete multimodal data, providing a scalable framework for disease stratification, biomarker discovery, and future precision medicine applications in AD.

items.title: Initiation of lenacapavir with dose escalation in a patient receiving rifabutin: A case report with therapeutic drug monitoring.
items.authors: McIntyre M, Tseng A, Cheung A, Leung F, Hempel A, Marzolini C, Devanathan AS.
items.abstract: Lenacapavir is a first-in-class HIV-1 capsid inhibitor with long-acting pharmacokinetics that enable 6-monthly subcutaneous dosing after initiation with oral lead-in. Lenacapavir is a CYP3A4, UGT1A1 and P-gp substrate; inducers of these enzymes and P-gp can significantly decrease lenacapavir concentrations. In patients receiving lenacapavir for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), supplemental lenacapavir doses can be administered if rifabutin (moderate inducer) or rifampin (potent inducer) are initiated. However, these recommendations have not been extended to lenacapavir when used for HIV treatment, and little is known about initiating lenacapavir in patients on stable therapy with inducers. We describe a 30-year-old man with advanced HIV infection and disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex infection receiving rifabutin and concurrent darunavir/ritonavir in whom lenacapavir was initiated with a 50% increase in both oral (900 mg on Days 1 and 2) and subcutaneous loading doses (1390.5 mg on Day 1). Therapeutic drug monitoring using validated UPLC-MS/MS method demonstrated that lenacapavir plasma concentrations remained above the target of 15.5 ng/mL (4× protein-adjusted 95% effective concentration [PA-EC<sub>95</sub>]) over the dosing interval, with C<sub>max</sub> of 245.7 ng/mL and a projected C<sub>min</sub> of 19.5 ng/mL at 6 months. HIV viral load remained suppressed. This case demonstrates that dose-adjusted lenacapavir can achieve therapeutic exposures in the presence of pre-existing moderate induction. These findings provide clinically relevant pharmacological insight to support the use of lenacapavir in complex patients requiring rifamycin therapy.

items.title: Retention in HIV Oral and Injectable HIV Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) Care in Milan, Italy.
items.authors: Raccagni AR, Tiani A, Capra N, Lolatto R, Loi G, Bruzzesi E, Muccini C, Maci C, Candela C, Castagna A, Nozza S.
items.abstract:
Background

The aims of this study are to estimate retention in HIV PrEP care in a large Italian centre and identify factors associated with discontinuation.

Setting

Tertiary infectious diseases centre in Milan, Italy.

Methods

This is a retrospective study including PrEP users with ≥1 follow-up visit between July 2017-January 2025; follow-up through June 2025. Retention was defined as ongoing follow-up at the centre or confirmed transfer while continuing PrEP; discontinuation as loss to follow-up (>12 months) or documented decision to stop PrEP. Users' characteristics were compared using non-parametrical tests. Kaplan-Meier method was used to assess retention probability.

Results

Among 1.781 PrEP users, 1.612 with ≥1 follow-up visit were included (median follow-up 1.7 years, IQR=0.7-2.9). Regimens at initiation were daily FTC/TDF (41.5%), on-demand FTC/TDF (58.3%), and long-acting cabotegravir (0.1%). Over follow-up, 77 users switched to cabotegravir. At data-freeze, 1142/1612 (70.8%) were in active follow-up, 22/1612 (1.4%) had transferred, 357/1612 (22.2%) were lost to follow-up, and 91/1612 (5.7%) had discontinued PrEP. The probability of retention was 84.7% (95%CI=82.9-86.6) at 1 year and 74.9% (95%CI=72.6-77.4) at 2 years. Older age (retained: 35.5 years, IQR=30.7-42.2 vs not retained: 32.9, IQR=28.6-38.0, p<0.001), DoxyPEP use (178/1164, 15.3% vs 17/448, 3.8%, p<0.001) and the number of STIs over follow-up (IRR 1.14, 95%CI=1.02-1.28, p=0.018) were associated with higher retention.

Conclusion

Retention in this Italian PrEP centre was moderately high. Older individuals and DoxyPEP users were more likely to be retained. These findings support targeted retention strategies and integrated sexual health services to reduce disengagement from PrEP care.

items.title: The Philadelphia TelePrEP Program: A Clinical-Public Health Partnership for Telehealth PrEP Delivery.
items.authors: Safa H, Nassau T, Brady KA, Spiegel N, Hernandez B, Williams J, Bonett S.
items.abstract: Inequities in HIV acquisition and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake persist in the United States. We present an innovative program that leverages telehealth to increase PrEP access through a unique public health and academic partnership. The Philadelphia TelePrEP Program (PTP) provides free, comprehensive, and accessible PrEP. Patients access the program through a public health sexual wellness website; patients are evaluated via telehealth, labs are completed using at-home testing kits or in-person at a local lab, and both oral and injectable PrEP modalities are prescribed through the program. Uninsured patients are covered through various patient assistance programs. We used patient data from the initial implementation of the PTP from October 2022 to December 2024 to describe the PrEP continuum to assess program reach and engagement by demographic groups. Of 576 unique individuals who scheduled appointments through the PTP website, 474 (82%) attended telehealth visits, 399 (69%) completed lab testing, and 386 (67%) were prescribed PrEP. Most patients who scheduled an appointment were cisgender men (85%), aged 18-34 (71%), and identified as non-Hispanic White (38%) or non-Hispanic Black (26%). Significant disparities in PrEP uptake emerged by gender (cisgender women: 39% vs. men: 70%), race/ethnicity (Black: 59% vs. White: 75%), and HIV risk group (MSM: 80% vs. heterosexual: 59%). The PTP successfully implemented a telehealth model for PrEP delivery, reaching a diverse cohort of Philadelphians. However, significant challenges to expanding access to telePrEP and PrEP more broadly remain, including lower rates of PrEP prescription for Black and Hispanic/Latine populations as well as cisgender women in the program.

items.title: Investigation of anti-SARS-CoV-2 multimeric bicyclic peptide inhibitors in a range of preclinical therapeutic settings.
items.authors: Harman MAJ, Gaynor KU, Papa G, Pellegrino S, Bezerra GA, McGuinness B, Jeffrey P, Beswick P, Stanway S, Van Rietschoten K, Chen L, Albecka A, Drulyte I, Herriott J, Kijak E, Gallardo-Toledo E, Tatham L, Sharma P, Bentley E, Sharp J, Kirby A, James LC, Owen A, Stewart JP, Skynner MJ.
items.abstract:
The spread of respiratory viruses, such as influenza and SARS-CoV-2, has presented significant challenges over the last 30 years, with few effective therapeutic options available to this day. Bicyclic peptides represent a unique, modular modality in the antiviral armamentarium against future pandemics. This study utilizes tool molecules to provide a deeper evaluation of multivalent bicyclic (Bicycle) molecule efficacy in several preclinical SARS-CoV-2 challenge settings. We explore both pre-exposure prophylaxis and post-exposure therapeutic settings via subcutaneous and intranasal routes of administration. We contextualize this further in bespoke scenarios where the immune system is compromised, as well as viral transmission. Promisingly, in all studies, we observe efficacy, significantly reducing infectious viral burden at each study endpoint. These data further support the candidacy of Bicycle molecules as a differentiated antiviral therapeutic class in the context of pandemic preparedness.

Importance

The COVID-19 pandemic triggered a rapid wave of innovation, accelerating the delivery of new vaccine technology and antiviral treatments. In our first paper, we described the discovery and molecular optimization of Bicycle molecules as a novel drug class for the potential treatment of SARS-CoV-2. Here, we have performed deeper characterization of these tool molecules in established animal models to evaluate scenarios for deployment, simulating SARS-CoV-2 transmission, testing more convenient delivery routes, such as intranasal, as well as looking at immunocompromised animals. The Bicycle molecules demonstrated positive outcomes in each of these studies and suggest that Bicycle molecules, as convenient and effective antiviral treatments, could be an important addition to help future preparedness against new viral pandemics.

items.title: Visible Light-Active Hyaluronic Acid Dermal Fillers for User-Demand Quick Molding and Local Drug Delivery.
items.authors: Jang S, Kang HG, Lee SO, Kim S, Seong KY, Choi HD, Song YS, An BS, Yang SY.
items.abstract: Injectable dermal fillers are increasingly used for tissue augmentation and local drug delivery, but conventional particulate fillers often require high injection forces, pose a risk of vascular occlusion, and offer limited moldability. Here, we report a visible light-responsive hyaluronic acid liquid dermal filler (HA photofiller) that enables on-demand molding and localized delivery of regenerative agents through biocompatible in-body photocrosslinking. The HA photofiller was prepared as a low-viscosity photocrosslinkable HA precursor that rapidly formed a mechanically stable hydrogel after short visible light exposure. Its liquid state allowed low-force injection (<3 N through a 27-gauge needle) and shaping before fixation, while the photocrosslinked hydrogels exhibited concentration-dependent mechanical tunability. Incorporation of α-ketoglutarate, selected as a regenerative agent that promotes collagen synthesis in dermal fibroblasts, enhanced dermal collagen deposition in vivo. The HA photofiller achieved rapid in situ fixation after molding, minimal initial swelling, excellent biocompatibility, and long-term volume maintenance (~90% retention over 28 d). In a rabbit ear intra-arterial injection model, the HA photofiller exhibited rapid vascular washout without visible signs of persistent vascular occlusion or ischemic tissue injury. By integrating on-demand moldability, improved vascular safety, and localized regenerative activity, this light-responsive HA photofiller provides a versatile platform for next-generation aesthetic and regenerative medicine applications.

items.title: Stated Choice Methods in Long-Acting and Extended-Release HIV Technologies: A Scoping Review of Methodological Practices and Translational Utility.
items.authors: Bauermeister JA, Golub S, Hosek S, Minnis A, Dubé K, Rael C, Krakower D, Lin W, Bangcaya C, Flexner C, Senn TE.
items.abstract:
Purpose of review

Long-acting and extended-release (LA/ER) technologies are expanding options for HIV prevention and treatment, but their population impact will depend on whether products and delivery models align with the priorities and constraints of intended users and providers. We reviewed how stated choice methods have been designed, analyzed, and used to generate implementation-relevant evidence for LA/ER technologies.

Recent findings

Fifty peer-reviewed studies published from 2020 to 2026 met inclusion criteria. Most examined HIV prevention (74%), enrolled end-users only (92%), and used discrete choice experiments or related variants (86%). Stakeholder-informed attribute sources were reported in 94%, but only 40% described dedicated, study-specific qualitative or advisory processes. Preference heterogeneity (94%), service-delivery attributes (80%), and structural access barriers (94%) were common. Only 22% included a respondent-specific status-quo comparator, 60% reported comprehension testing, and 4% achieved moderate-to-high representativeness. Although 84% examined pipeline-aligned attributes, reporting did not establish whether those attributes remained modifiable at the relevant product-lifecycle stage. Only four studies included providers, and treatment-preference research was concentrated in high-income settings. Methodological sophistication does not ensure translational utility. Stated choice studies should align their attributes, sampling, and choice architecture with the decision-maker, the product's lifecycle stage, and the decisions still open to change. As products mature, research should prioritize actionable delivery, access, and health-system decisions and validate preferences against product experience and observed behavior.

items.title: Factors associated with HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis uptake among female sex workers in Karongi District, Rwanda: a retrospective cross-sectional study
items.authors: Twagirimana G, Nshimiyimana E.
items.abstract: Background Oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is highly effective in preventing HIV acquisition, yet its uptake among key populations in sub-Saharan Africa remains suboptimal, and evidence on PrEP uptake among female sex workers (FSWs) in Rwanda outside Kigali is limited. This study aimed to determine the proportion of PrEP uptake and the factors associated with it among FSWs in Karongi District, Rwanda. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using routine data on eligible HIV-negative FSWs aged 17 years or older screened for PrEP between March and December 2021 at the 10 PrEP-providing health facilities in Karongi District. PrEP uptake was defined as initiation between first eligible screening and 31 December 2021. Factors associated with uptake were identified using multivariable logistic regression and modified Poisson regression, reported as adjusted prevalence ratios (APR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), and robustness was assessed in sensitivity analyses. Results Of 800 eligible FSWs, 265 (33.1%) initiated PrEP. Uptake was associated with recruitment by community volunteers (APR 3.4, 95% CI 1.7–7.2), being single (APR 1.7, 95% CI 1.3–2.3), being a farmer (APR 1.6, 95% CI 1.3–2.1), HIV testing in the previous 3 months (APR 1.7, 95% CI 1.3–2.1), having 3–4 sexual partners in the previous 7 days (APR 1.4, 95% CI 1.1–1.7) and prior awareness of PrEP (APR 2.1, 95% CI 1.5–2.9); these associations were consistent in direction across sensitivity analyses. Uptake also varied markedly by sector of residence, and the association with health insurance differed by sector, being positive in Rubengera and negative in Bwishyura; the final model, which assumed a single insurance effect across sectors, was therefore misspecified for insurance, and its pooled insurance estimate is not interpreted. Conclusions Only one in three eligible FSWs in Karongi District initiated PrEP early in PrEP implementation.
