Volunteer-led demand creation and offering PrEP at HIV testing warrant evaluation as strategies to improve uptake as PrEP services, including long-acting PrEP, are scaled up. The role of health insurance, which differed by sector, warrants further investigation.

items.title: Implementing HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) among cisgender female sex workers: A worldwide scoping review to guide the future research agenda for HIV prevention.
items.authors: Plazy M, Becquet V, Amador-Paz S, Nouaman M, Maouhoub E, Meertens C, Mouquin R, Youssoufa H, Coffie P, Larmarange J.
items.abstract: Female sex workers (FSWs) experience a disproportionately high burden of HIV. To inform future research and policy efforts on HIV prevention, this study synthesizes global evidence on HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) among cisgender FSWs worldwide. This scoping review was conducted using six multidisciplinary databases searched up to December 2024. Titles and abstracts, then full texts, were independently screened. Data extraction comprised i) general study characteristics (UNAIDS region, country, study type, outcomes, type of PrEP, and study years), ii) detailed data of each outcome (including PrEP knowledge, a priori acceptability - interest, and effective acceptability - use, retention and adherence). Drivers and barriers to PrEP acceptability were analyzed using an adapted conceptual framework encompassing six domains: patient characteristics, individual knowledge and perceptions, medication-related factors, social processes, structural and health system factors, and sex work characteristics. After selection, 120 eligible studies were identified, mostly conducted in Eastern and Southern Africa. PrEP knowledge was initially low but increased quickly once programs were introduced. PrEP interest was consistently high across regions, driven by perceived HIV risk and desire for self‑protection. PrEP uptake, retention and adherence varied widely. Main barriers included sex work realities (i.e., unstable housing, alcohol use), social processes (i.e., stigma), individual characteristics (i.e., mobility), treatment-related characteristics (i.e., side effects), and health system challenges (i.e., clinic access constraints). Drivers included social support and reminder tools. While evidence on long‑acting PrEP remained limited, interest was consistently high as reducing daily burden. Overall, the findings support a socio-ecological understanding of PrEP engagement among FSWs, including the sex work context as a distinct intermediary layer. They highlight the need for differentiated and structurally responsive PrEP delivery models tailored to the realities of sex work. Expanding long‑acting PrEP options and improving service accessibility, community engagement, and stigma reduction strategies will be critical to strengthening HIV prevention among FSWs globally.

items.title: Integrating Cost Considerations into HIV Care and Prevention to Achieve Population-Level Outcomes.
items.authors: Golden MR, Cannon CA, Menza TW, Sharma M, Porter KM, Dombrowski JC.
items.abstract: The US government currently spends >$29 billion annually on HIV treatment, but only 69% of people with diagnosed HIV (PWH) in the US are virally suppressed, a failure partially related to poverty. Medical providers preferentially treat HIV using higher cost medications, and use of higher cost drugs for PrEP is increasing. New, long-acting antiretrovirals (ARVs) have the potential to improve prevention and care while further increasing costs. We believe that the US approach to HIV should change to increase the use of lower cost HIV medications and promote the selective use of long-acting ARVs to treat people who cannot achieve viral suppression using oral drugs. A portion of the money saved through more efficient medication utilization management should be used to improve access to care and provide socioeconomic support to low-income PWH. Together, these changes have the potential to decrease costs, improve health outcomes, and better align spending with patient preferences.

items.title: CAB-LA PrEP Prescriptions and Abandonment in the United States, January 2022-June 2025.
items.authors: Zhu W, Patel RR, Huang YA, Davis NL, Hoover KW, Kourtis AP.
items.abstract:
Background

Injectable long-acting cabotegravir (CAB-LA) for HIV preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2021. A national assessment of CAB-LA PrEP abandonment, defined as not filling any prescription, could inform national PrEP implementation efforts.

Methods

We conducted a national observational cohort study using IQVIA Longitudinal Prescription data to characterize persons prescribed CAB-LA or daily oral PrEP (DO-PrEP) in the United States during January 2022-June 2025. We compared 6-month abandonment risk among individuals with an index CAB-LA or DO-PrEP prescription during 2022-2024. Associations were estimated using multivariable modified Poisson regression models and reported as adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

The number of individuals prescribed CAB-LA PrEP increased from 4,645 in 2022 to 23,378 in 2024 and 25,018 during January-June 2025. The proportion of individuals receiving CAB-LA increased from 0.1% in quarter 1 of 2022 to 5.4% in quarter 2 of 2025. While women had a higher 6-month PrEP abandonment risk than men, regardless of PrEP regimen, they were less likely to abandon CAB-LA (11.9%) than DO-PrEP (18.1%, aRR=0.68, 95% CI: 0.62-0.74). The opposite was observed for men, with men more likely to abandon CAB-LA PrEP (10.2%) than DO-PrEP (8.1%, aRR=1.25, 95% CI: 1.20-1.31).

Conclusions

CAB-LA PrEP prescribing increased steadily during the first 3.5 years after approval; abandonment risk differed by PrEP regimen and sex. Addressing barriers to injectable and daily oral PrEP uptake, and strengthening sex-specific PrEP implementation strategies, may further reduce abandonment risk.

items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Cabotegravir Long-Acting HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP): A Systematic Review of Modelling Studies.
items.authors: Effiong FB, Olawuyi DA, Effiong BB, Adeyemi AV, Ekpor E, Dine RD, Inaku KO.
items.abstract:
Objectives

Cabotegravir long-acting injectable (CAB-LA) is a promising non-oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention, especially where daily oral adherence is poor. Despite superior efficacy, CAB-LA's high price raises concerns about economic value and implementation across settings. This study reviewed modelling studies on CAB-LA's cost-effectiveness as PrEP across diverse populations and settings.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase and Cochrane Library (2015-2025), assessing CAB-LA's cost-effectiveness versus oral PrEP or no PrEP. Eligible studies reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, cost per HIV infection averted, or cost per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) or disability-adjusted life year gained. Reporting quality was assessed using the CHEERS 2022 checklist. Results were narratively synthesized due to heterogeneity.

Results

Eleven modelling studies across sub-Saharan Africa, the United States, and Asia-Pacific showed that CAB-LA averted more HIV infections than oral PrEP, especially in high-incidence, low-adherence populations. In high-risk U.S. populations, CAB-LA averted about 71,000 infections and gained 4.65 million QALYs. In Africa, CAB-LA became economically favourable under lower acquisition-cost assumptions, although cost-effective prices varied across models, populations, price years and thresholds. U.S. and Asia-Pacific models found CAB-LA not cost-effective at current prices, requiring 24-88% price reductions. Sensitivity and scenario analyses showed that cost-effectiveness estimates were responsive to CAB-LA price, HIV incidence, ART coverage, adherence, persistence, and programme-delivery assumptions.

Conclusion

CAB-LA cost-effectiveness is context dependent and generally more favourable at lower prices, higher-incidence populations, and poor oral PrEP adherence. Wider adoption may require strategies to improve economic value, equitable access, and implementation, especially in resource-constrained settings.

items.title: Real-world durability of long-acting cabotegravir PrEP in choice-driven and indication-driven users.
items.authors: Moschese D, Esvan R, Fusetti C, Micheli G, Lazzarin S, Farinacci D, Giacomelli A, Barchi V, Cossu MV, Giacinta A, Oreni L, Caruso F, Antinori A, Gori A, Mazzotta V.
items.abstract:
Objectives

To evaluate real-world adherence, persistence, and discontinuation of CAB-LA PrEP among individuals accessing this strategy either by choice or due to clinical or behavioural indications associated with challenges to oral PrEP.

Methods

We conducted an observational cohort study including 388 individuals initiating CAB-LA PrEP between December 2024 and November 2025 at two Italian referral centres. Adherence to the injection schedule, persistence over time, and all-cause and drug-related discontinuations were assessed overall and stratified by access modality.

Results

Adherence exceeded 94.9% across almost all assessed injection time points. Overall persistence remained high, with 87.9% (95% CI 84.7-91.2%) of participants remaining on CAB-LA PrEP at week 52 [84.1% (95% CI 77.0-91.3%) in choice- and 89.3% (95% CI 85.7-92.9%) in indication-driven users; P = 0.191]. All-cause discontinuation occurred in 12.1% of participants, while drug-related discontinuations were uncustomary (6.9%).

Conclusions

CAB-LA PrEP demonstrated high adherence, sustained persistence, and low rates of drug-related discontinuation in routine clinical practise. Durable performance regardless of access modality supports its feasibility both as a preference-sensitive option and as an alternative for populations experiencing difficulties with oral prevention.

items.title: Equitable expansion of PrEP Choice for transgender women and travestis in Brazil: Community and other stakeholder perspectives on implementation opportunities
items.authors: Zamudio-Haas SA, Saggese GSR, Barros D, Cezaretto A, Prado PV, Rodriguez J, Menezes NP, Veras MA, Lippman SA.
items.abstract: Expanding prevention programs to incorporate new PrEP modalities could offer important benefits to transgender women and travestis (TWT) in Brazil, who are underserved by current approaches. Long-acting injectable (LAI) products are not yet available through the national health system, and episodic PrEP was recently approved for some TWT, providing a critical window for formative research to guide equitable rollout. Engaging the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research, we interviewed TWT PrEP consumers (8), PrEP providers (8), and program/policy advisors (4) in São Paulo. Participants expressed enthusiasm for offering all modalities as a cohesive ‘PrEP choice’ intervention– despite consensus on advantages of LAI-products (increased ease, freedom, protection) and limitations of episodic PrEP (complicated dosing, limited eligibility). We differentiated implementation opportunities related to culture, learning climate, and readiness in neighborhood primary care clinics, referral centers, and community-based programs. Findings coalesced around the need to center community in planning and executing implementation processes, by incorporating adjunctive interventions (pain management, peer navigation, food and transportation assistance) and peer staff. By interviewing stakeholders who participated in LAI-PrEP research, we elicited informed perspectives grounded in lived experience, before widespread availability. Findings provide a foundation for future studies comparing implementation and outcomes for TWT in different delivery settings.

items.title: Reported use of participatory methods in health research with transgender and gender diverse populations: a scoping review.
items.authors: Kerr L, Booth K.
items.abstract:
Introduction

It is well established that health promotion is most effective when informed by the community it targets, through participatory methods. Transgender and gender diverse peoples have been marginalized and experience worse health and lower levels of service access when compared with cisgender individuals. The use of participatory methods in health research to address these issues is of high importance to help rectify this. The aim of this scoping review was to document the reported use of participatory methods in health research with transgender and gender diverse samples to map the current applications of these research frame works and priorities for future studies.

Methods

The inclusion criteria for articles were published January 2014-February 2025, peer-reviewed, health research, transgender and gender diverse populations, English language, and participatory methods. Three databases were searched: CINAHL complete, MEDLINE complete and LGBTQ+ source. Articles were independently screened for eligibility. Consensus meetings were held to synthesize results.

Results

Forty-two papers were identified in the search that met inclusion criteria. The majority of studies were conducted in the United States (n = 23, 54.76%) and other high-income countries, ranging in time duration from several weeks to years, and commonly had as their research topic gender affirming care (n = 9, 21.42%), mental health and wellbeing (n = 9, 21.42%) and healthcare experiences (n = 8, 19.04%). Whilst most studies employed numerous strategies of community participation, a significant proportion (n = 14, 33.33%) of studies did not report having a community reference group. The aims of studies could be clustered under three broader categories; to understand or describe; to develop or evaluate; and research priority setting.

Conclusions

Studies were heterogeneous and more rigorous application of participatory principles and reporting of methods is needed. Research with transgender and gender diverse populations must include their meaningful participation from inception to completion. Greater detail and clarity in reporting is necessary to aid future studies who can build on the successes and shortfalls of previous studies.

items.title: Bridging the gap: HIV epidemiologic patterns and PrEP use inequities over the past decade in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
items.authors: Coelho LE, Torres TS, Cardoso SW, Jalil EM, Coutinho C, Struchiner CJ, Goedert GT, Genari J, Grinsztejn B, Veloso VG, Luz PM.
items.abstract:
Background

In 2017, Brazil integrated Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) into its unified health system. This study aimed to analyze temporal trends in key HIV epidemiological indicators over the past decade to explore the extent to which PrEP expansion has influenced HIV diagnosis rates. We investigated whether disparities in PrEP use across demographic groups were temporally associated with differences in HIV incidence at the populational level.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective analysis of public surveillance data (2012‒2024) for Rio de Janeiro city, Brazil. We estimated annual trends in the proportion of people living with HIV, HIV identifications rates, ART coverage, viral suppression, and PrEP use, stratified by sex, age, race, and education. We used time-series analysis with 3-year moving averages and segmented regression models to identify significant trend changes and breakpoints.

Results

Exponential growth in PrEP use was observed from 2017‒2024, with PrEP use surpassing the number of new HIV identifications after 2021. Despite this expansion, HIV identification rates increased among most demographic subgroups since 2020, particularly among young, Black, and Pardo individuals. PrEP expansion disproportionately benefited older individuals rather than those aged 18‒24 years. Black individuals constituted the smallest racial group using PrEP. Males with ≥12-years of education accessed PrEP at rates nine times higher than males with the lowest education level.

Conclusions

Oral PrEP alone may be insufficient to curb HIV transmission without addressing structural barriers including racism, educational inequities, homophobia, and transphobia. Future prevention efforts should combine different PrEP modalities, community-centered approaches, anti-racism initiatives, LGBTQIAPN+-affirming care, and targeted outreach to younger populations.

items.title: Lenacapavir in the Treatment and Prevention of HIV-1 Infection: A Narrative Review of Clinical Efficacy and Resistance Selection Risk.
items.authors: Tasbas U.
items.abstract: Lenacapavir is a first-in-class HIV-1 capsid inhibitor. By acting on a structural protein rather than a viral enzyme, it inhibits several stages of the replication cycle and shows no cross-resistance with the available drug classes; a half-life of 8-12 weeks after subcutaneous administration allows a six-monthly regimen. A narrative review was conducted, searching PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov up to July 2026 and drawing on phase 2 and phase 3 trials, structural and modelling studies, and regulatory documents. In virologically suppressed adults undergoing a planned regimen switch, the week-48 treatment differences for bictegravir/lenacapavir (ARTISTRY-1 and ARTISTRY-2) and for weekly oral islatravir/lenacapavir (ISLEND-1 and ISLEND-2) ranged from -1.0 to 0.3 percentage points, with the upper bound of each 95% confidence interval lying below the prespecified non-inferiority margin of 4 percentage points. These are investigational switch regimens: lenacapavir itself is currently approved only for multidrug-resistant HIV-1 infection and for pre-exposure prophylaxis, whereas neither the bictegravir/lenacapavir nor the islatravir/lenacapavir combination has yet been authorised. In multidrug-resistant infection, 85% of participants in CAPELLA had HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL at week 156 when missing data were excluded. In prevention, no infection occurred among the 2,134 participants in the lenacapavir arm of PURPOSE 1 (0.00/100 person-years; incidence rate ratio vs background: 0.00, 95% CI: 0.00-0.04), whereas the incidence in the emtricitabine-tenofovir alafenamide arm did not differ from the background incidence (incidence rate ratio: 0.84, 95% CI: 0.55-1.28). The pharmacokinetic property that gives lenacapavir its strength is argued to be, at the same time, its principal vulnerability. As a pharmacological concern, the subtherapeutic concentration tail can create a state of functional monotherapy in which resistance may be selected when the virus replicates at concentrations that suppress the wild-type but not a resistant variant (the mutant selection window). Modelling predicts de novo resistance 106-235 days after the last injection and, for N74D and the double mutants, a selection window overlapping even the steady-state concentrations of the six-monthly regimen, so that these mutants may be selected not only during the post-discontinuation tail but also while dosing continues as planned. Resistance actually observed in clinical studies has been limited and conditional: N74D arose in the two participants infected in the lenacapavir arm of PURPOSE 2 despite expected drug concentrations, and in CAPELLA every participant who developed resistance had a background regimen that was inactive or inadequately taken, indicating that the vulnerability is manageable. Lenacapavir therefore requires careful patient selection, fully active companion drugs, and a planned discontinuation strategy.

items.title: Therapeutic and Prophylactic Agents for Viral Diseases: Current Status, Challenges, and Future Prospects.
items.authors: Khan S, Nisar A, Li X, Yu H, Qadeer A, Mehmood SA, Lamraoui I, Liu S, Zhu L, Deng X, Kong B, Zhong K, Xia Z.
items.abstract: Viral diseases remain a major global health challenge despite substantial advances in vaccination, antiviral therapeutics, and public-health interventions. However, current antiviral strategies are still constrained by important gaps, including rapid viral evolution, limited broad-spectrum efficacy, immune escape, antiviral resistance, incomplete durability of protection, and inequitable global access to prevention and treatment. This review provides a comprehensive and integrated overview of contemporary antiviral prevention and therapeutic strategies, spanning vaccines, monoclonal antibodies, direct-acting antivirals, host-targeted therapies, immunomodulators, RNA-based therapeutics, gene-editing technologies, and cellular immunotherapies. We discuss the mechanistic foundations, clinical applications, pharmacologic considerations, and translational challenges associated with each modality across major human viral pathogens, including HIV, HBV, HCV, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, RSV, Ebola virus, arboviruses, and herpesviruses. Particular emphasis is placed on emerging innovations such as long-acting prophylaxis, Fc-engineered monoclonal antibodies, nanoparticle and mucosal vaccine platforms, CRISPR-based antiviral systems, and broadly protective host-directed approaches designed to overcome resistance and enhance pandemic preparedness. In addition, we highlight the growing importance of real-time genomic surveillance and equitable global deployment strategies in shaping future antiviral responses, collectively underscoring that the next generation of antiviral medicine will depend on the convergence of universal immunization strategies, durable therapeutics, precision immune modulation, and rapidly deployable platform technologies capable of addressing both endemic and emerging viral threats.

items.title: A Randomized, Double-Blind Phase 1 Safety and Pharmacokinetic Study of Q-Griffithsin Douche Administered Rectally to HIV-1 Seronegative Adults (the PREVENT Study).
items.authors: Ho K, Edick S, Zyhowski A, Swistok A, Meyn L, Rohan L, Wang L, Matoba N, Lasnik A, Fuqua J, Spiegel H, Hartman D, Brand RE, Cranston RD, McGowan I, Palmer K, Brand RM.
items.abstract: The availability of oral and long-acting injectable pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) has transformed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) prevention; however, some individuals may prefer behaviorally congruent, nonsystemic, on-demand rectal PrEP options that avoid chronic systemic exposure. The Q-Griffithsin (Q-GRFT) rectal douche is a novel, user-controlled PrEP candidate, containing a natural (red alga-derived), potent broad-spectrum antiviral lectin for pericoital rectal use. This first-in-human Phase 1 trial evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics (PKs), pharmacodynamics (PDs), and acceptability of a single Q-GRFT rectal douche dose. Sixteen HIV-negative participants (eight female and eight male) with a history of recent receptive anal intercourse were enrolled in this randomized, double-blind study. Following single-dose administration, blood, rectal fluid, and rectal tissue samples were collected for safety, PK, and PD analyses using an ex vivo rectal explant HIV challenge model. Acceptability was measured using structured questionnaires. The Q-GRFT douche was safe with no Grade 3 or 4 adverse events or significant histological abnormalities. Acceptability was high at 93% of the study product. At 1 h postdose, geometric mean (range) Q-GRFT concentrations were 522.18 ng/mL (52.8-12,482.2) in rectal swab eluate and 6.85 µg (0.80-51.07) in rectal tissue, declining over 24 h. Q-GRFT was not detectable in plasma. Higher individual tissue drug levels correlated with reduced HIV infectivity in both rectal eluate (p = 0.036) and tissue explant (p = 0.003). In this first-in-human study, a single administration of Q-GRFT as a rectal douche demonstrated favorable safety, acceptability, and high local drug exposure without systemic absorption, supporting further evaluation as an on-demand, nonsystemic rectal PrEP strategy.

items.title: Modelling minimum resource requirements to reach Ending the HIV Epidemic (EHE) goal in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
items.authors: Morojele NK, Yeo YR, Shenoi S, Jeetoo M, Su J, Charles DL, Moll A, Mbaya J, Zama P, Gasa S, Bloem C, Braithwaite RS.
items.abstract:
Introduction

KwaZulu-Natal (KZN), South Africa's provincial HIV epicentre with a prevalence of over 20%, strives to accelerate progress toward the global End the HIV Epidemic (EHE) 2030 goal. This modelling study aimed to maximize HIV prevention in KZN, given resource constraints.

Methods

We performed allocative efficiency analyses (i.e. identifying the allocation of resources that maximizes benefits) with an HIV compartmental transmission model calibrated to HIV prevalence and incidence in KZN since 1990, under two perspectives, 1) "status quo," building on 2022 funding and coverage levels and allocating additional resources, and 2) "perfect reallocation," shifting resources toward more efficient interventions before allocating additional resources. Outcomes included infections averted, quality-adjusted life years added, time to reach the EHE goal, and annual programmatic costs.

Results

With "status quo," KZN will fall short of the 2030 EHE goal by approximately 500,000 infections, requiring additional annual expenditures of US$355 million across 11 interventions, from greatest to least efficiency: long-acting PrEP; HIV self-testing; DREAMS; index testing; VMMC; defaulter tracing; community-based testing; differentiated care; condom distribution, ART adherence support for detectable viral load; and oral PrEP. Alternatively, a "perfect reallocation" strategy that shifts funds from lower-efficiency to higher-efficiency interventions could avert 240,000 additional infections, narrowing the EHE gap by nearly half and reducing additional annual expenditures to US$344 million to close the gap.

Conclusions

KZN will require additional resources to achieve its 2030 EHE goals, but strategic prioritization and reallocation toward more efficient interventions can maximize HIV prevention within resource constraints.

items.title: Transition From Oral to Long-Acting Injectable Preexposure Prophylaxis: Comparative Levels of Cabotegravir, Tenofovir, and Emtricitabine in Plasma and Seminal Fluids.
items.authors: Sabetta E, Raccagni AR, Mattino A, Ferrari D, Brignoli A, Bruzzesi E, Muccini C, Castagna A, Locatelli M, Nozza S.
items.abstract:
Background

Although oral preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF)/emtricitabine (FTC) is highly effective for individuals whose sexual activities place them at high risk for HIV infection, it is limited by adherence. Long-acting injectable cabotegravir (CAB-LAI) offers an alternative, but limited data are available on its distribution in seminal fluid (SF), a key vector for sexual HIV transmission. In this study, the pharmacokinetics of antiretrovirals in the blood plasma (BP) and SF of HIV-negative men who have sex with men during the transition to CAB-LAI were characterized.

Methods

Forty-four men who have sex with men initiated on CAB-LAI at San Raffaele Hospital (January-May 2025) were enrolled. At baseline (T0), 23 of the participants were on daily TDF/FTC, 18 were on event-driven TDF/FTC, and 3 were PrEP naïve. Oral PrEP users continued TDF/FTC for 7 days after the first injection. BP and SF samples were collected at 0 (T0), 7 (T1), 30 (T2), and 90 (T3) days after injection. The drug levels were quantified using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. HIV testing was performed longitudinally.

Results

At T0, the median TDF levels were 31 ng/mL in BP and 152 ng/mL in SF, whereas the median FTC levels were 79 ng/mL in BP and 676 ng/mL in SF. At T1, both drugs remained detectable in fewer participants, with consistently higher levels in SF. By T2, both drugs had largely decreased in level, with isolated detectable cases, and neither drug was measurable at T3. The median BP CAB concentration was 1844 ng/mL at T1, with 80% of the men exceeding the protective 664 ng/mL threshold. This proportion remained high at T2 (77.3%) and T3 (60.6%). By contrast, the SF CAB concentrations were approximately 100-fold lower.

Conclusions

Most participants achieved BP-protective CAB levels within 1 week, confirming sustained efficacy. However, CAB was often below the detection limit in SF.

items.title: Extended in vivo activity of VRC01 HIV-1 prophylaxis entails initial protective efficacy and subsequent breakthrough infections.
items.authors: deCamp AC, Juraska M, Li L, Magaret CA, Williamson BD, Bai H, Huang Y, Giorgi EE, Zhang L, Carpp LN, Edupuganti S, Mgodi NM, Gillespie K, Haddock B, Gonzales P, Cabello R, Orrell C, Lama JR, Laher F, Lazarus EM, Sanchez J, Frank I, Hinojosa JC, Sobieszczyk ME, Mukwekwerere PG, Makhema J, Baden LR, Seaton KE, Hural J, McElrath MJ, Takuva S, Randhawa AK, Kochar N, Piwowar-Manning E, Donnell DJ, Sista N, Andrew P, Karuna ST, Kublin JG, Gray GE, Cohen MS, Barouch DH, Tomaras GD, Rolland M, Montefiori DC, Morris L, Mullins JI, Williamson C, Corey L, Gilbert PB.
items.abstract: The two parallel antibody-mediated prevention (AMP) efficacy trials evaluated whether intravenous infusion of the anti-CD4 binding site broadly neutralizing antibody VRC01 prevents HIV-1 acquisition. Here, we analyzed HIV-1 acquisition in AMP through the week 104 final study visit. Against viruses considered highly sensitive to VRC01 [80% inhibitory concentration (IC<sub>80</sub>) < 1 microgram/milliliter], VRC01 prophylaxis maintained cumulative prevention efficacy of 66.3% (95% confidence interval: 32.4, 83.2%), suggesting that the antibody successfully blocked or cleared these infections. In the post-week 80 period (after the final dose at week 72), HIV diagnosis and resistance to VRC01 were more frequent and greater in the VRC01 groups versus placebo. For instance, more HIV diagnoses with viruses considered moderately sensitive or resistant to VRC01 (IC<sub>80</sub> ≥ 5 microgram/milliliter) were made in the VRC01 groups compared with placebo groups (11 versus 1). Plausibly, as in vivo VRC01 concentration waned, suppressed viruses-often evolving greater resistance because of selective pressure-emerged as detectable infections. Our findings suggest that, whereas single antibodies can block sensitive strains, multiple antibodies are likely required to prevent both viral escape and breakthrough infections.

items.title: Mobile Units for Integrated Addiction and HIV Prevention Services for People Who Inject Drugs: The HPTN 094 Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.authors: Shoptaw S, El-Bassel N, Hanscom B, Skalland T, Denis C, Goodman-Meza D, Kuo I, Lake JE, Morrison EAB, Richards AM, Fogel JM, Richardson P, Marzinke MA, Clarke W, PaulChoudhury R, Harris-Wisecarver J, Cummings M, Chandler R, Burwen DR, Andrew P.
items.abstract:
Importance

Integrated models to deliver HIV preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD) for people who inject drugs are needed.

Objective

To determine whether integrated PrEP and MOUD services delivered on a mobile unit with manualized peer navigation improved PrEP and MOUD use compared with peer navigation to existing community-based services.

Design, setting, and participants

This 2-group, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted between May 2021 and September 2024 in Houston, Texas; Los Angeles, California; New York, New York; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; and Washington, DC, among people aged 18 years and older currently injecting drugs, without HIV, with OUD, and not taking MOUD but willing to consider MOUD.

Interventions

The intervention arm (n = 203) consisted of 26 weeks of manualized peer navigation plus integrated PrEP, MOUD, and limited clinical and supportive services delivered on a mobile unit. The active control arm (n = 206) consisted of 26 weeks of manualized peer navigation to available community-based PrEP, MOUD, harm reduction, and supportive services.

Main outcomes and measures

The co-primary outcomes were PrEP use and MOUD use at 26 weeks. Secondary outcomes included PrEP and MOUD use at 52 weeks, HIV incidence, and all-cause mortality.

Results

Of 842 people who inject drugs who were screened, 409 were randomized: 134 (32.8%) female; 146 (11.2%) aged 30 years and younger vs older than 30 years. At the 26-week visit, the intervention and active control arms were similar for confirmed PrEP use: 11/203 (5.4%) vs 6/206 (2.9%) and MOUD use: 30/203 (14.8%) vs 22/206 (10.7%), respectively. At the 52-week visit, intervention and active control arms were similar for confirmed PrEP and MOUD: 4/203 (2.0%) vs 4/206 (1.9%) and MOUD use: 27/203 (13.3%) vs 29/206 (14.1%). One HIV acquisition occurred in the intervention and 2 in the active control arms; HIV incidence rate of 0.9 per 100 person-years (95% CI, 0.2-2.6). Four deaths were confirmed in the intervention arm and 13 in the active control arm (hazard ratio, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.1-0.9; P = .03).

Conclusions and relevance

In this randomized clinical trial, mobile delivery of integrated HIV prevention, addiction, and navigation services did not improve primary outcomes beyond peer navigation alone. The significantly lower all-cause death rate at 52 weeks in the intervention arm bears replication for delivering integrated PrEP and MOUD services to people who inject drugs.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04804072.

items.title: Congenital Syphilis in South Africa: A Narrative Review of Epidemiology, Health System Drivers, Prevention, and the Path to Elimination.
items.authors: Phiri S, Skepu A, Nxumalo Z, Letsielo MJ, Oyekunle V.
items.abstract: Congenital syphilis (CS), caused by vertical transmission of Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum, remains a major but preventable cause of foetal and neonatal morbidity and mortality globally. Despite established antenatal screening programmes and the availability of effective treatment with benzathine penicillin G (BPG), South Africa continues to experience a substantial burden of maternal and congenital syphilis, with a 2023 national case rate approximately four times the World Health Organization (WHO) elimination target. This narrative review synthesises evidence from peer-reviewed publications, national surveillance reports, and policy documents identified through systematic searches conducted up to September 2026 [searched through August 2026] on congenital syphilis in South Africa. It addresses the microbiology and pathogenesis, epidemiology, clinical burden, diagnostic approaches, health system determinants, and strategies for elimination. Persistent transmission is associated with documented gaps in antenatal booking, repeat screening, treatment completion and partner management, and with recurrent benzathine penicillin shortages; HIV co-infection, poverty and other social and structural factors are likely contributors, but direct evidence for them is more limited. Congenital syphilis remains associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes including miscarriage, stillbirth, prematurity, neonatal mortality, and long-term disability. The elimination of congenital syphilis in South Africa requires strengthening antenatal care coverage, universal and repeat syphilis screening, prompt and complete maternal treatment, partner services, enhanced surveillance systems, and closer integration with HIV programmes. Progress towards the country's 2028 elimination target will depend on a coordinated health systems approach aligned with WHO triple-elimination validation criteria.

items.title: Optimizing Preexposure Prophylaxis Adherence: Evaluating Point-of-Care Urine Tenofovir Testing and Tailored Counseling Among Young South African Women.
items.authors: Poovan N, Velloza J, Ndlovu NH, Meisner A, Grabow C, Gandhi M, Donnell D, Hosek S, Celum C, Delany-Moretlwe S.
items.abstract: Among South African women using oral HIV preexposure prophylaxis, we compared a urine tenofovir point-of-care test with dried blood spot tenofovir diphosphate concentrations for recent vs longer-term adherence and assessed acceptability. The test demonstrated 76% accuracy, 100% sensitivity, and 69% specificity for high adherence (tenofovir diphosphate ≥700 fmol/punch) and was highly acceptable. Clinical Trials Registration: NCT04038060.

items.title: Beyond HIV prevention: Reframing PrEP clinics as hubs for viral hepatitis prevention and elimination.
items.authors: De Maria F, Branda F, Fusco P, Ceccarelli G, Scarpa F, Ciccozzi M, Russo A.
items.abstract:
Objectives

The expansion of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) has created a growing network of prevention services that regularly engage people who may also be exposed or susceptible to viral hepatitis. PrEP care is inherently longitudinal, involving repeated clinical assessment, laboratory testing, counselling and vaccination review. These features make PrEP clinics uniquely positioned to contribute to viral hepatitis prevention and elimination. In this narrative review, we synthesize evidence on the integration of viral hepatitis prevention, screening, diagnosis and care within PrEP services, and propose a practical framework, the PrEP-viral hepatitis elimination cascade, for translating the principle of integrated HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infection services into routine clinical practice.

Methods

A focused literature search was conducted between 1 May and 8 August 2026 across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and the WHO Global Index Medicus, using documented search strings supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists. We prioritized studies conducted among PrEP users or within PrEP programmes, together with relevant international guidelines and policy documents. Records were screened in two stages against predefined eligibility criteria, and the findings were mapped to the steps of the cascade. Evidence was sought on HAV and HBV vaccination coverage, HBV seroprevalence and susceptibility, the relationship between tenofovir-based PrEP and HBV prevention, HCV epidemiology among PrEP users, simplified diagnostic strategies and integrated service delivery models. Given the heterogeneity of study designs and outcomes, the literature was synthesized narratively rather than through formal meta-analysis. Interventions and indicators for each cascade step were then summarized in an evidence-linked implementation and monitoring table.

Results

The evidence consistently demonstrates that vaccination gaps for HAV and HBV persist among PrEP users, with suboptimal initiation and completion rates across settings; that HBV susceptibility remains common among individuals entering PrEP care; and that tenofovir-based PrEP, while offering incidental HBV protection, should not substitute for vaccination. HCV epidemiology among PrEP users is heterogeneous, supporting risk-adapted testing strategies, while simplified diagnostic pathways and self-testing approaches have shown promise for HCV. The PrEP-viral hepatitis elimination cascade proposed here offers a structured, implementable framework connecting vaccination, case finding, linkage to care and longitudinal reassessment within the existing PrEP pathway. The cascade is presented as a detailed figure and as an implementation and monitoring table linking each step to supporting evidence, candidate interventions and measurable indicators, without assigning responsibilities to specific providers. Implementation challenges include variability in PrEP delivery models, the need for equity-oriented approaches and the implications of long-acting and tenofovir-sparing PrEP regimens for HBV prevention.

Conclusion

PrEP programmes have created a longitudinal prevention infrastructure that extends beyond HIV prevention. HAV vaccination, HBV screening and vaccination, identification of chronic HBV infection, HCV testing, simplified diagnostics, treatment linkage and surveillance for reinfection can all be incorporated at different points of the PrEP pathway. The next step is to move from opportunistic to intentional integration. PrEP clinics should be reframed as integrated viral hepatitis prevention and elimination hubs, translating global strategies into routine care and contributing to viral hepatitis elimination goals. The question is no longer whether PrEP clinics can contribute to viral hepatitis elimination, but whether the global health community will deliberately invest in making this integration a reality.

items.title: Molecularly Imprinted Polymer Biosensors for Sustainable Antiretroviral Drug Monitoring.
items.authors: Animashaun C, Slaughter G.
items.abstract: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) have transformed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) treatment and prevention, but both depend on sustained adherence and accurate drug-exposure monitoring. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry remains the reference method for antiretroviral quantification, but centralized instrumentation and multistep sample preparation limit decentralized, same-visit testing. This review evaluates molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) as synthetic recognition elements for optical and electrochemical antiretroviral sensing, situated within the broader case for green analytical chemistry in decentralized HIV care. MIP-based platforms are compared with direct electrochemical detection and aptamer-based sensing across selectivity, stability, fabrication complexity, regeneration, and matrix tolerance in plasma, dried blood spots, urine, saliva, and interstitial fluid. Although recent MIP sensors achieve nanomolar detection, none of the reviewed studies report standardized greenness metrics such as AGREE, GAPI, or the Analytical Eco-Scale, limiting comparison of their true environmental performance. Clinical value remains further constrained by limited validation in authentic specimens, nonspecific adsorption, and batch-to-batch variability. Future progress will depend on simpler MIP architectures, safer extraction chemistries, matrix-matched validation, and systematic sustainability assessment using established green analytical chemistry metrics.

items.title: Optimizing HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis among transgender women in the United States: a conceptual framework of engagement in prevention-effective adherence
items.authors: Cooney E, Kaptchuk RP, Saleem HT, Stevenson M, Aguayo-Romero RA, Reisner SL, Wirtz AL.
items.abstract: Transgender women in the United States experience a disproportionate burden of HIV driven by multi-level social and structural vulnerabilities. Although oral PrEP, injectable cabotegravir, and twice-yearly lenacapavir are now available, PrEP use remains suboptimal. We conducted a qualitative analysis of 18 semi-structured life history calendar interviews conducted between February and June 2022 with transgender women in the eastern and southern United States who were indicated for PrEP and had varied PrEP histories. We generated a conceptual framework of prevention-effective adherence based on findings. Two bidirectional domains, capacity to safely engage with the healthcare system and compatibility between PrEP and individual values and preferences, shaped prevention-effective adherence. Influencing both domains were distal factors, including stigmas, identity-based oppression and marginalization, and sociostructural context. Unlike models that categorize barriers using existing frameworks, our inductively derived framework specifies how factors relate to each other, centers prevention-effective adherence rather than discrete cascade steps, and situates PrEP engagement in the life course. Our findings illuminate modifiable factors, including cost, availability of gender-affirming care, and access to evidence-based HIV/STI information, to improve and optimize PrEP engagement among transgender women in the United States.

items.title: Special Issue: Abstract Supplement HIV Glasgow 8-11 November 2026, Glasgow, UK/Virtual.
Revisiting trial design considerations to improve efficiency of HIV-1 vertical transmission prevention efficacy trials in infants.
items.authors: Giganti MJ, Wu D, Ruel T, Abrams EJ, Yin DE.
items.abstract:
Introduction

While the global incidence of HIV-1 vertical transmission has reduced greatly, a persistent and unacceptable number of new infant infections continue to occur through breastfeeding. Long-acting antiretroviral agents, including injectable drugs and broadly neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, given as prophylaxis to infants hold great potential to eliminate HIV-1 transmission. However, given the low frequency of HIV-1 vertical transmission during breastfeeding in trial settings, efficient and innovative study designs will be necessary to evaluate the efficacy of agents administered to infants as prophylaxis.Key Design Considerations:We provide an overview of study design considerations and assess alternative specifications that may improve the efficiency of future trials to evaluate the efficacy of a novel agent administered to infants in preventing breastfeeding acquisition of HIV-1. We highlight key attributes of the study estimand (intervention, target population, outcomes and endpoints, intercurrent events, and population-level summaries) and discuss nuances in their specification with respect to improving efficiency. We explore alternatives to the classic randomized clinical trial framework, including augmented clinical trials that incorporate external data to supplement clinical trial data. We also provide an overview of Bayesian and transportability-based statistical analysis approaches for analyzing such augmented clinical trials. Modifications to the study design in the context of the estimand framework alone will not be sufficient to address challenges introduced by the low frequency of transmission events. Alternative study designs that incorporate external data are becoming increasingly acceptable and may help alleviate resource constraints.

Conclusion

A multi-faceted approach will be required to design efficacy trials for postnatal prophylaxis. This work provides a guide for thinking through key study design decisions.

items.title: Brief Report: Long-acting Injectable Preexposure Prophylaxis Preference for Persons Who Use Drugs and Are Involved with the Criminal Legal System.
items.authors: Springer SA, Di Paola A, Kuo I, Knight K, Nijhawan AE.
items.abstract:
Background

criminal legal involved (CLI) persons who use drugs are at high risk of exposure to HIV, yet few initiate preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP). Understanding interest in PrEP and the different formulations of PrEP may improve uptake in this population.

Methods

Participants were CLI adults aged 18 or older, used opioids and/stimulants, tested negative for HIV, and met Centers for Disease Control and Prevention PrEP eligibility criteria. Characteristics of persons interested in PrEP were compared with those who were not interested in PrEP at baseline. Among those interested in PrEP, characteristics were compared for those who preferred long-acting injectable (LAI) vs oral PrEP.

Results

Of 566 persons enrolled, 35.1% (N = 199) were interested in PrEP; of those, 60.8% (N = 121) preferred LAI vs 39.1% (N = 78) preferred oral PrEP. PrEP interest was greater in persons from Texas (50%) vs Connecticut (18.3%). A significantly higher odds of being interested in PrEP was associated with having a methamphetamine use disorder and a higher self-perceived risk of HIV; and a history of sharing injection drug use equipment was associated with a higher odds of being interested in LAI vs oral PrEP.

Conclusions

Among CLI persons who use drugs eligible for PrEP, persons in TX, were more interested in PrEP compared with persons in CT. Persons with a methamphetamine use disorder and a higher self-perceived risk of HIV were predictors of PrEP interest and sharing injection drug use equipment was a predictor of interest in LAI vs oral PrEP. More research on patient choice and shared decision making should be included to improve PrEP initiation.

items.title: Modeling the Potential Impact of Scaling Up Event-Driven PrEP Among Gay, Bisexual, and Other Men Who Have Sex With Men.
items.authors: Chandra C, Maloney KM, Le Guillou A, Hoover KW, Jenness SM.
items.abstract:
Background

Event-driven preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) (EDP), or PrEP taken around the time of sex, could be a preferred option over daily PrEP among cisgender gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (MSM). However, recommendations for EDP versus daily dosing require consideration of optimal strategies for HIV prevention based on heterogeneous behavioral and biological PrEP indications.

Methods

We used network-based mathematical HIV transmission modeling to understand the potential population-level impact of implementing EDP alongside daily PrEP using the 2-1-1 dosing schedule: 2 pills on the day of sex, 1 pill a day after, and 1 pill 2 days after. We simulated HIV transmission among 100,000 MSM in Atlanta, Georgia over 10 years. Compared with a baseline scenario with only daily PrEP and no EDP, we tested counterfactual scenarios that increased EDP use by changing initiation rates, expanding EDP to MSM not indicated for daily PrEP, and targeting EDP among MSM with low daily PrEP adherence who discontinued daily PrEP.

Results

Increasing EDP initiation such that overall PrEP use was nearly double that at baseline (28.5% vs. 16.1%) yielded a percent of infections averted (PIA) of 18.3%. Expanding eligibility for EDP to any sexually active MSM resulted in a PIA of 15.8%. Targeting EDP for MSM discontinuing PrEP did not yield population-level improvements. Increasing initiation of EDP had a greater impact on PIA compared to improving EDP adherence.

Conclusions

Using EDP to improve overall PrEP use resulted in reductions in HIV incidence, whereas targeted EDP initiation for MSM with low daily PrEP adherence did not improve outcomes over 10 years.

items.title: Differentiated obesity treatment: Pharmacological CRF2 agonism drives fat loss, skeletal muscle hypertrophy and improved glucose metabolism in preclinical obesity.
items.authors: Niss K, Lundh S, Patel R, Fels JJ, Gruhler A, Madsen SH, Chimienti F, Bau S, Åsberg D, Lykke L, Cox N, Wulff BS, Roed NK, Li C, Christoffersen BØ.
items.abstract:
Objective

Loss of lean mass during weight reduction may compromise metabolic health and physical function. Urocortin 2 (UCN2) activates corticotropin-releasing factor receptor 2 (CRF2) and has been linked to beneficial effects on skeletal muscle and glucose metabolism. We evaluated an acylated UCN2 analogue (acyUCN2), alone or combined with an acylated GLP-1 analogue (acyGLP-1), in preclinical obesity models.

Methods

Diet-induced obese (DIO) Sprague Dawley rats and DIO Göttingen Minipigs were treated with vehicle or acyUCN2 (rats, pigs) or acyGLP-1 or combination therapy (rats only). Food intake, body weight (BW), body composition, glucose tolerance and energy expenditure (rats only) were assessed. Histology and RNA-sequencing were used to characterize muscle remodelling and transcriptional responses.

Results

In rats, acyUCN2 reduced food intake and fat mass, increased lean mass and muscle weight, and improved glucose tolerance despite limited effects on BW. Energy expenditure was not affected. Histology demonstrated hypertrophy across fibre types and a shift from type 2A to type 2X/B fibres. Transcriptomic analyses supported muscle growth and fibre type switch, relative reduced vasculature, regulation of neuromuscular junction-associated genes, and overlap to human acute exercise-response signatures. In obese minipigs, acyUCN2 increased lean mass and improved insulin sensitivity, with modest effects on BW and fat mass, alongside regulation of genes linked to muscle biology and metabolism.

Conclusions

Pharmacological CRF2 agonism promotes favourable body composition, muscle hypertrophy, and improved glucose metabolism despite limited weight loss, supporting clinical development of UCN2 analogues as a differentiated obesity treatment, particularly in combination with appetite-regulating therapies and in settings where preservation of functional muscle mass is critical.

items.title: Comparison of subcutaneous and intravenous administration of the monoclonal antibody CSX-1004 on fentanyl-induced respiratory depression in squirrel monkeys.
items.authors: Kumar M, Burke EL, Zang Y, Sharma A, Bremer PT, Desai RI.
items.abstract:
Background

Fentanyl and related synthetic opioids remain major contributors to overdose mortality, primarily through opioid-induced respiratory depression. CSX-1004 is a fully human monoclonal antibody designed to bind fentanyl in the peripheral circulation and prevent its entry into the brain. This study evaluated the pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) equivalence of intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) administration of CSX-1004 in squirrel monkeys and established a population PK (PopPK) model to support route extrapolation.

Methods

Protection against fentanyl-induced respiratory depression was assessed after administration of 40 mg/kg CSX-1004 using whole-body plethysmography over 28 days. Serum antibody concentrations were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and PK parameters were characterized using noncompartmental and PopPK analyses.

Results

Both IV and SC administration produced substantial and durable attenuation of fentanyl-induced respiratory depression, resulting in a greater than 10-fold rightward shift in fentanyl potency that persisted for up to 28 days. SC CSX-1004 administration exhibited a maximum concentration of 491.7 ± 50.4 μg/mL at 48.0 ± 19.6 h (Tmax) and an absolute bioavailability of 92.0% based on AUC0-∞ . Terminal half-life was comparable between routes (∼272 h). A two-compartment PopPK model with first-order absorption and elimination adequately described the concentration-time data and demonstrated robust predictive performance. Serum concentrations and respiratory protection were lower after SC than after IV administration during the first 24-48 h, reflecting the absorption phase, and converged from Day 2 onward. Simulations indicated that SC and IV administration achieved overlapping systemic exposures beyond the absorption phase and equivalent concentrations associated with sustained respiratory protection through Day 28.

Conclusion

These findings demonstrate that SC administration of CSX-1004 provides PK and PD outcomes comparable to IV dosing, once absorption is complete, supporting SC delivery as a practical and clinically feasible approach for long-acting prophylaxis against fentanyl-induced respiratory depression.

items.title: Adhesive hydrogel-mediated spatiotemporal delivery of garlic-derived nanovesicles reprograms immunometabolism to rescue periodontal bone regeneration.
items.authors: Yu C, Yu X, Cao P, Liu Y, Chen L, Wang X, Zhang D, Ma Y, Cai Y, Zhang Y, Cai Q, Luan Q.
items.abstract: The core challenge in regenerating inflammatory bone defects, such as periodontitis-related bone resorption, lies in the dysregulation of the immune-metabolic microenvironment, which required implanted materials to simultaneously possess tissue sealing properties, sustained immune modulation capacity and metabolic intervention functions. Herein, garlic-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (GaELNs), exhibiting anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities, are embedded in an injectable, tissue-adhesive polyethylene glycol hydrogel (GaE-PEG) to meet the challenges. The hydrogel exhibited favorable tissue adhesion and sustained release of GaELN-associated protein in vitro. GaE-PEG promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated periodontal ligament stem cells, GaE-PEG alleviated mitochondrial oxidative stress, restored oxidative phosphorylation, suppressed excessive glycolysis, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses linked these effects to mitochondrial metabolic regulation, while oligomycin treatment attenuated the osteogenic response, supporting a contribution of oxidative phosphorylation. In a rat model of periodontitis-related bone defects, GaE-PEG reduced local inflammation and promoted alveolar bone regeneration, with improved regenerative outcomes compared with a single local injection of free GaELNs at an equivalent dose and Bio-Gide™/Bio-Oss™ treatment. These findings support an adhesive hydrogel strategy integrating local nanovesicle delivery with immunomodulation and metabolic regulation to promote bone regeneration under inflammatory conditions.

items.title: Discrepancies in Adverse Event Reporting Between ClinicalTrials.gov and Publications in HIV/AIDS Clinical Trials: A Pre-Post Analysis of the FDAAA Final Rule.
items.authors: Langerman R, Jameison GN, Corwin L, Archer D, Keefer K, Hazlitt R, Harris T, Ford AI, Vassar M.
items.abstract:
Background

Adverse event reporting is critical for interpreting and applying findings from HIV/AIDS clinical trials. Although registries such as ClinicalTrials.gov provide structured safety data, clinicians and guideline developers often rely primarily on peer-reviewed publications, which may selectively report harms. Prior research across multiple specialties has documented incomplete or inconsistent adverse event reporting in publications relative to registry entries, including incomplete reporting of serious harms. The consistency of adverse event reporting between registries and publications in HIV/AIDS trials has not been systematically evaluated.

Main body

We conducted a registry-to-publication comparison study of interventional HIV/AIDS trials with results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov between September 27, 2009, and December 31, 2024. Corresponding publications were identified through ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed, and Google Scholar. Eligible studies were Phase 2-4 (or not applicable), enrolled individuals living with HIV, evaluated therapeutic, preventive, or adherence-related interventions, and had both publicly posted registry results and a full-length English-language publication. Two independent reviewers extracted adverse event data using a standardized form. Outcomes included serious adverse events, other adverse events, treatment discontinuations, and mortality. Among 129 eligible trials, 62% showed mismatched serious adverse event counts between registry entries and publications, with registries more often reporting higher counts. An additional 28% of trials failed to report serious adverse event counts in either source - a distinct category of dual-source non-reporting. Across all reporting domains, registries more consistently reported complete safety data than publications. Following implementation of the 2017 Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act Final Rule, reporting improved within ClinicalTrials.gov (serious adverse events reported in 74% of trials) but remained low in publications (26%). Regression analyses demonstrated a significant increase in overall adverse event reporting completeness after the Final Rule (p < 0.001). Sponsor type was not associated with reporting completeness, whereas larger enrollment was associated with modestly lower completeness (p = 0.02).

Conclusion

Substantial discrepancies persist between registry and publication reporting of adverse events in HIV/AIDS trials. Regulatory requirements were associated with changes in registry reporting patterns but did not eliminate inconsistencies in the published literature. Greater alignment between registry and journal reporting standards is needed to strengthen the transparency and reliability of safety evidence.

items.title: Early patient-reported outcomes and planned persistence with lenacapavir for HIV preexposure prophylaxis in routine clinical care.
items.authors: Hazra A, Multani A, Vail R, Sukumaran S, Smith R, Halbur D, Patel RR.
items.abstract: This multicenter study evaluated early patient-reported outcomes (PROs) among individuals initiating twice-yearly lenacapavir (LEN) for HIV preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) in routine care. Convenience, driven by reduced dosing frequency, was the primary motivation for LEN initiation, and overall satisfaction was high despite frequent but generally mild injection-site reactions. Persistent nodules and pain emerged as the leading patient-reported concerns regarding future continuation, highlighting the importance of patient-centered counseling and implementation strategies to optimize long-term persistence with long-acting PrEP.

items.title: Implementation of long-acting injectable PrEP at a Latine community organization: protocol for a mixed-methods, hybrid type 3 implementation-effectiveness study.
items.authors: Cutshaw MK, Navarro I, Barfield R, Krajewski T, Kilpatrick KW, McKellar MS, Poteat T.

items.title: Interpreting antiretroviral exposure and drug-drug interactions in pregnancy: A clinically anchored framework for HIV pharmacology.
items.authors: Eke AC.
items.abstract: In pregnancy, antiretroviral drug-drug interactions must be interpreted against dynamic changes in gastrointestinal physiology, plasma-protein binding, renal elimination, hepatic enzyme activity and membrane transporter expression. Interaction studies quantify geometric mean exposure ratios relative to nonpregnant adults, but these measures describe relative pharmacokinetic change rather than whether effective exposure is preserved. For HIV treatment, validated exposure-response targets remain reasonable starting anchors when pregnancy-specific targets are unavailable. No evidence indicates that gestational immune adaptation alone requires a different intrinsic antiviral target. Pregnancy alters target attainment by altering drug disposition and variability, and it can modify the pharmacokinetics of both the victim antiretroviral and the perpetrator drug. For long-acting injectable PrEP, protective exposure, dosing interval and pharmacokinetic tail require separate consideration from treatment targets. This review evaluates candidate evidentiary anchors, including protein-adjusted in vitro inhibitory concentrations, exposure-response relationships, therapeutic drug-monitoring targets and model-informed probability of target attainment. Evidence from integrase inhibitors, protease inhibitors, non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, tenofovir formulations and long-acting agents demonstrates that similar proportional reductions in exposure can have different clinical implications depending on therapeutic margin, resistance barrier, interaction mechanism, formulation and pharmacologically relevant matrix. A newly proposed six-domain framework integrates clinical context, active analyte, exposure metric, evidentiary anchor, distributional target attainment and clinical outcomes. Physiologically based and population pharmacokinetic models provide evidence when pregnancy-specific data are unavailable, but their use should reflect model verification and uncertainty. The central objective is therefore not to define a universal pregnancy threshold but to determine whether pharmacologically effective exposure is maintained in the setting of gestational physiology and concomitant medicines.

items.title: Awareness of and Hypothetical Willingness to Use Long-Acting Injectable Cabotegravir and Associated Factors Among Oral Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis Users Who Obtained the Medicine Online in China: Web-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Li Q, Zhou J, Huang S, Zhang Y, Zheng J, Ruan C, Zou H, Ren X, Xu J, Tang H, Xu Y, Zhao Z, Xue H, Cheng F, Luo S.
items.abstract:
Background

Oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is highly effective for HIV prevention, but its real-world impact depends on sustained adherence. Long-acting injectable cabotegravir (CAB-LA) may reduce the burden of daily or event-driven pill use. In China, many oral PrEP users obtain medication online, but little is known about their prior CAB-LA awareness or willingness to consider it.

Objective

This study assessed prior CAB-LA awareness, hypothetical willingness to use CAB-LA, reported barriers and facilitators, and associated factors among oral PrEP users in China obtaining PrEP online.

Methods

This cross-sectional study analyzed baseline data from the Real-world E-consumer Cohort of Oral PrEP (RECOPE), a prospective cohort in China. Participants completed a self-administered web-based questionnaire assessing prior CAB-LA awareness, hypothetical willingness after standardized CAB-LA information, sociodemographic characteristics, recent sexual behaviors and sexually transmitted infection (STI) diagnosis, and oral PrEP-related characteristics. Modified Poisson regression with robust SEs estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) and adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% CIs. Primary regression analyses were restricted to sexually active participants.

Results

Among 621 oral PrEP users, the mean age was 29.9 (SD 6.4) years; all were assigned male sex at birth, and 608 (97.9%) identified as men. Overall, 216 of 621 (34.8%, 95% CI 31.1%-38.6%) participants reported prior CAB-LA awareness. After receiving standardized information, 428 of 621 (68.9%, 95% CI 65.2%-72.4%) participants expressed hypothetical willingness to use CAB-LA if it became available in China. Convenience was the most frequently reported facilitator among willing participants (395/428, 92.3%), whereas high cost was the most frequently reported barrier among those who did not express willingness (123/193, 63.7%). In adjusted analyses, event-driven PrEP users had a lower prevalence of prior CAB-LA awareness than daily PrEP users (aPR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50-0.86), whereas participants who had switched oral PrEP regimens in the past 3 months had higher prior awareness (aPR 1.34, 95% CI 1.07-1.68). Hypothetical willingness was more prevalent among participants reporting an STI diagnosis in the past 3 months (aPR 1.22, 95% CI 1.08-1.39) and chemsex (aPR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26), whereas higher PrEP-related stigma was associated with slightly lower willingness (aPR 0.99 per 1-point increase, 95% CI 0.98-0.99).

Conclusions

Among oral PrEP users in China obtaining PrEP online, prior CAB-LA awareness was limited, whereas hypothetical willingness was common after standardized information was provided. Prior awareness differed by oral PrEP regimen and recent regimen switching, whereas willingness was associated with recent STI diagnosis, chemsex, and PrEP-related stigma. Convenience was a major appeal, while cost remained an important barrier. These findings support improving access to balanced PrEP information and addressing practical barriers as long-acting PrEP becomes more widely available.

items.title: Editorial: The prevention of HIV among adolescent girls and young women: leaving no one behind.
items.authors: Moyo E, Dzinamarira T.

items.title: Expanded polling booth surveys monitor HIV programme outcomes among female sex workers and men who have sex with men in Nairobi, Kenya.
items.authors: Bhattacharjee P, Isac S, Kimani J, Emmanuel F, Kabuti R, Kinyua A, Ndukuyu VN, Musyoki H, Kiplagat A, Arimi P, Shaw SY, Gandhi M, Blanchard J, Becker ML, McClarty LM.
items.abstract:
Introduction

Nairobi County has the largest HIV prevention programme for female sex workers (FSW) and men who have sex with men (MSM) in Kenya. Routine monitoring of programme outcomes is critical for tracking progress toward programme targets. Monitoring approaches need to be rapid, affordable, and sufficiently robust to capture programme outcomes while meaningfully involving communities.

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional outcome assessment among FSW and MSM (71% reporting sex work) in Nairobi County from April-July 2023 using an expanded polling booth survey (ePBS). The ePBS combined anonymous group-level polling booth survey (PBS) with an individual biobehavioural survey (BBS) to assess behavioural, structural and biological outcomes. Weighted descriptive analyses summarised programme outcomes.

Results

The target sample size for the study was 769 FSW and 420 MSM. Overall, 759 FSW (response rate 98.6%) and 398 MSM (response rate 94.7%) participated in 64 PBS sessions; 758 FSW completed the BBS, while 398 MSM completed the behavioural component and 396 completed the biological component. Condom use at last sex was reported by 80.8% of FSW with paying clients and by 72.7 and 68.9% of MSM with non-regular partners and paying clients, respectively. Recent peer educator contact was reported by 68.8% of FSW and 65.8% of MSM. Healthcare-related stigma was reported by 8.0% of FSW and 7.5% of MSM, and recent forced sex by 10.7% of FSW and 6.5% of MSM. HIV prevalence was 14.0% among FSW and 18.6% among MSM. Among participants living with HIV, 85.9% of FSW and 80.4% of MSM were virally suppressed. Among those reporting current oral PrEP use, tenofovir was detected in urine among 48.3% of FSW and 52.6% of MSM.

Conclusion

FSW and MSM in Nairobi remain priority populations for the HIV response. The findings suggest persistent gaps across behavioural, structural and biomedical outcomes that need to be addressed. The ePBS approach offers a practical and scalable method for generating actionable outcome data that can complement routine monitoring systems and support adaptive HIV programming. As countries face increasing pressure to optimise HIV programmes within constrained funding environments, approaches that generate timely and actionable outcome data will become increasingly important.

items.title: The Bidirectional Effects of Gender-Affirming Hormone Therapy and Preexposure Prophylaxis in Transgender Individuals.
items.authors: Blumenthal J, Goyal R, Mischel A, Gianella S, Burke L, Dube MP, Hoenigl M, Chow K, Silva J, Moore D, Haubrich R, Corado K, Anderson PL, Bolan R, Morris S.
items.abstract: Transgender individuals both on and off gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) had similar preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) concentrations after 12 weeks of daily oral emtricitabine-tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (FTC/TDF) PrEP use. Hormone concentrations were not significantly different with or without FTC/TDF PrEP, and there were no changes in the perceived effect on GAHT in those taking PrEP.

items.title: A Highly Sensitive and Specific Rapid Lateral Flow Assay for the HIV Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors Bictegravir, Cabotegravir, and Dolutegravir.
items.authors: Wei X, Youngpairoj AS, Haaland R, Dinh C, Patel HK, Perez JJ, Brown K, Vanderford TH, Johnson JA.
items.abstract:
Background

Second-generation HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitors (INSTIs)-bictegravir (BIC), cabotegravir (CAB), and dolutegravir (DTG)-are leading components of highly potent antiretroviral therapy, and CAB is also used for long-acting chemoprevention. Rapid detection of clinically relevant INSTI concentrations could support point-of-care assessment and real-time clinical decision-making. We developed a lateral flow assay (LFA) that detects BIC, CAB, and DTG in whole blood and plasma and evaluated its performance against predefined concentration thresholds and high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).

Methods

A single LFA cassette design was developed using a monoclonal antibody to distinguish BIC, CAB, and DTG concentrations below trough, at minimal-to-moderate trough, and at ideal concentrations. LFA results were read visually at 20 min and were compared with LC-MS/MS-quantified INSTI concentrations for 124 clinical plasma specimens.

Results

For 24 plasma samples from US participants receiving treatment involving one of the three INSTIs, the LFA interpretations matched all LC-MS/MS results except for one DTG specimen, which was interpreted by LFA as 1.0-1.6 μg/mL but measured 2.1 μg/mL by LC-MS/MS. Among 100 plasma remnants from routine national surveillance in Eswatini, the LFA correctly interpreted DTG concentrations in 95 specimens. Four specimens had DTG LC-MS/MS concentrations slightly above the LFA-determined range, differing by ≤ 0.1 μg/mL, and one specimen measured at 1.20 μg/mL by LC-MS/MS was interpreted as ≥ 1.6 μg/mL by LFA. In total, 6 of 124 specimens (4.8%) had LFA-interpreted INSTI concentrations that varied slightly from the LC-MS/MS results, with no statistically significant difference in overall performance by Wilcoxon signed-rank test (W = 8.00, p = 0.94, one-tailed).

Conclusions

The LFA design successfully provided clinically useful interpretations of BIC, CAB, and DTG concentrations with minor discrepancies in < 5% of samples. Importantly, all low-concentration samples of < 1 μg/mL were correctly interpreted by LFA. The assay shows promise as a point-of-care tool for assessing clinically relevant INSTI concentrations.

items.title: Aspects of Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis Empowerment and Pitfalls Among Racial and Ethnic Young Men Who Have Sex With Men.
items.authors: Salazar R, Emetu RE, Missari S.
items.abstract: HIV continues to disproportionately affect men who have sex with men (MSM), particularly Black and Latino populations. With pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) now central to HIV prevention efforts, understanding perceptions of safer sex practices among racial and ethnic minority MSM is essential. This qualitative study conducted three focus groups with 22 Asian, Black, and Latino MSM aged 18 to 29 in Los Angeles County between January and April 2022 to explore how safer sex has evolved since PrEP's Food and Drug Administration approval in 2012. Four themes emerged: (a) shifting definitions of safer sex, (b) sexual autonomy and empowerment, (c) peer perceptions and stigma surrounding PrEP use, and (d) provider judgment and limited knowledge. Participants described PrEP as a source of sexual agency but also highlighted ongoing stigma and discomfort when disclosing PrEP use or engaging with health care providers. Although all participants were active PrEP users, broader access disparities remain, particularly for MSM of color. The recent Food and Drug Administration approval of a biannual injectable PrEP offers a promising opportunity to expand uptake by reducing stigma, enhancing convenience, and improving adherence. These findings underscore the need for culturally responsive messaging, supportive clinical environments, and policy efforts to ensure equitable PrEP access for marginalized MSM. Public health practitioners and providers can use this insight to improve HIV prevention strategies and tailor interventions to the lived experiences of MSM of color.

items.title: "I Feel Like I Am a Winner:" High Levels of Autonomous Decision-Making Among Women Receiving HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) Choice Counselling in Sub-Saharan Africa.
items.authors: Segawa I, Sisel H, Kyampire C, Wilcher R, Charles KL, Jeckonia P, McGuire C, Kekana A, Naidoo N, Mahaka I, Kadama H, Irungu E, Fonner V, CATALYST study (Catalyzing access to new prevention products to stop HIV).
items.abstract: As pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) options expand, providers play a critical role in supporting clients to select the method that best meets their needs. We examined how client-provider interactions during PrEP choice counselling influenced women's autonomous decision-making and early continuation on PrEP. CATALYST was a mixed-methods study that delivered an informed choice of oral PrEP, the dapivirine vaginal ring, and injectable cabotegravir among women attending 28 public-sector facilities in Kenya, Lesotho, South Africa, Uganda, and Zimbabwe. We analysed cohort data collected between June 2024 and January 2025 and adapted a family planning Autonomous Decision-Making (ADM) scale into a six-item PrEP-specific measure (PrEP-ADM scale). Factor analysis assessed scale structure, and logistic regression identified factors associated with fully autonomous decision-making (PrEP-ADM score of 18/18) and refilling PrEP within three months. Twenty-six in-depth interviews explored counselling experiences. Among 2,488 women, 92% reported fully autonomous decision-making. Two subscales were identified: "communicating information" and "supporting informed choice". Women in sero-different partnerships had higher odds of reporting fully autonomous decision-making (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 1.63, 95% CI: 1.11-2.39), whereas pregnant (aOR: 0.29, 95% CI: 0.17-0.47) and breastfeeding women (aOR: 0.46, 95% CI: 0.28-0.76) had lower odds. Autonomous decision-making was not associated with PrEP refill. Qualitative findings confirmed clear information exchange and supportive counselling, although pregnant and breastfeeding women described more constrained choices. High levels of perceived autonomous decision-making were observed, though further work is needed to refine these measures and identify the essential elements of informed PrEP choice counselling.

items.title: Corrigendum to "Provider Perspectives on the Delivery of Long-Acting PrEP for HIV Prevention to Men Who Have Sex with Men and Who Use Methamphetamine".
Willingness to Use HIV Pre-exposure Prophylaxis among Community Pharmacy Users in Uganda
items.authors: Nakate V, Odongpiny EAL, Hamill MM, Onzia AA, Melendez JH, Reynolds SJ, Castelnuovo B, Parkes-Ratanshi R, Manabe YC, Kiragga AN.
items.abstract: HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake is limited in Uganda. Participants were recruited from 18 Kampala community pharmacies (CP); 52.2% had sexually transmitted infection (STI) symptoms, and 62.2% were females. Of the 424 participants with negative or unknown HIV status, only 127 (30.0%) were aware of PrEP; 91.0% reported willingness to use oral and 58.5% injectable PrEP. Preferences for PrEP delivery were at a community pharmacy (44.8%), health facility (48.7%), and home (6.6%). Use of CPs for distribution could increase PrEP uptake.

items.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis awareness, interest, and modality preferences to prevent HIV among cisgender women in the Dominican Republic and the United States.
items.authors: Kerrigan D, Davis W, O'Rourke A, Galai N, Mantsios A, Scott RK, Moriarty P, Metzner AA, Oglesby A, Karver TS, Taggart T, Barrington C, Uhrig Castonguay BJ, Yonamine K, Gomez H, Perez M, Donastorg Y.
items.abstract:
Introduction

Significant inequities in HIV incidence and prevalence exist among cisgender women (hereafter women), including a disproportionate burden of the epidemic among Black women in the United States and female sex workers globally. Women have limited awareness of and access to pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV pharmacoprevention.

Methods

We explored PrEP awareness, interest, and modality preferences [daily oral vs. long-acting injectable (LAI) PrEP] in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic (DR) and Washington, DC (DC) in the United States through in-depth interviews (IDIs) with women (N = 40) and healthcare providers (HCPs; N = 20) in 2021-2022 and surveys of women (N = 602) in 2022-2023. Thematic analysis andmultivariate regression were utilized.

Results

Across settings, women were aged ≥18 years and HIV-negative; most were Black or multiracial, single, in their 30s, with >1 child. In IDIs, women characterized PrEP as an empowerment tool and welcomed modality options; HCPs across sites relayed a lack of comfort and preparation to address the unique needs of women and discuss LAI PrEP. In surveys, women reported low PrEP awareness and use: 29% (DC) and 6% (DR) had heard of daily oral PrEP, <6% had heard of LAI PrEP across sites, and 3% (DC) and 1% (DR) had ever used PrEP. Strong interest in taking PrEP varied (DC, 5%; DR, 80%). Modality preferences were similar, with most preferring LAI vs. daily oral PrEP (DC, 73%; DR, 71%). Across sites, preference for LAI PrEP was inversely associated with concern for injection pain/tenderness. In DC, LAI preference was associated with a higher score on a PrEP optimization/ considerations scale.
