In the DR, LAI preference was associated with injectable medication/contraception experience and alcohol use and inversely associated with PrEP stigma and partner violence.

Discussion

Diverse groups of women have shared and unique drivers of PrEP modality preferences which should be considered when developing and tailoring multi-level interventions to promote PrEP awareness and uptake among women. These interventions should address social determinants and side effects and include HCP training and tools that promote shared decision-making.

items.title: Advances in HIV-1 Envelope-Based Vaccine Development.
items.authors: Chan KW, Jiang X, Wang AL, Kong XP, Wu X.
items.abstract: As the sole viral protein expressed on the surface of viral particles and infected cells, the HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein is the most important target for vaccine development. Structurally defined sites of vulnerability recognized by broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) serve as major targets for vaccine design, including V1V2 apex, V3 base glycan, CD4-binding site, fusion peptide, and membrane proximal external region. Although well-established for affinity-matured antibody binding and antigenicity, these sites are not necessarily immunogenic. Three approaches have been undertaken to work around this problem: stabilizing native-like trimers, targeting bNAb germlines, and developing booster immunizations based on envelope-bNAb coevolution. With these approaches, breakthroughs have been made in vaccine-elicited neutralization gaining breadth, thus supporting certain immunogens and regimens over others. Here, from the perspectives of HIV-1 envelope and antibody genetics as well as structures, we systematically review the most recent advances in envelope-based vaccines and their remaining barriers. We also summarize lessons learned about HIV-1 envelope immunogenicity and discuss potential strategies for future development.

items.title: Brief Communication: Oral pre-exposure prophylaxis history and willingness to use injectable HIV prevention among clients at two Ugandan clinics
items.authors: Olet SC, Muluga WU, Musoki D, Kihumuro BR, Farid M, Ssebandeke I, Among F, Nait C, Mulyowa A, Stecher CD, Kiwanuka SN, Musoke D.
items.abstract: We compared hypothetical willingness to use injectable pre-exposure prophylaxis among 116 HIV prevention-service clients at two Ugandan clinics. Willingness was 81.8% among current oral users, 42.4% among former users and 50.0% among never users. Compared with current users, age- and sex-adjusted prevalence ratios were 0.52 (95% confidence interval 0.34–0.78) and 0.60 (0.39–0.92), respectively. Neutral responses were common among former and never users. These findings support assessing information needs across oral-use histories and testing whether counselling and a real product offer translate stated willingness into initiation and continued use.

items.title: A Dissociation-Based Seahorse XF Workflow for Quantifying Averaged Bioenergetics in Anchorage-Independent Cancer Cell Clusters.
items.authors: Lindeque R, Visagie JL, Fouché BR, Labuschagne CF.
items.abstract: Cell clustering during anchorage-independent growth (AIG) is a key hallmark of malignant progression, supporting survival under detachment during metastatic dissemination. However, bioenergetic profiling of cell clusters grown under AIG conditions remains technically challenging, in part because of steep nutrient and oxygen gradients and irregular cell cluster shapes that complicate Seahorse XF assay normalization. Here, we present a dissociation-based Seahorse XF96/XF Pro method that enables high-throughput quantification of the average bioenergetic state of anchorage-independent cancer cell clusters. In this workflow, clusters generated in ultra-low adherent plates are enzymatically and mechanically dissociated into a single-cell suspension immediately prior to Seahorse XF Mito Stress Test analysis on poly-D-lysine-coated 2D microplates. This approach ensures that all viable cells throughout each cluster contribute equally to oxygen consumption rate (OCR) measurements and reduces the need for complex post hoc normalization. We further apply this workflow to an in vitro metastasis model in which A549 lung cancer cells are studied as attached, detached (anchorageindependent), and reattached populations, mimicking primary tumor cells, circulating/clustered cells, and secondary lesions, respectively. Detached cells exhibit reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and diminished basal and maximal OCR, whereas reattached cells largely restore membrane potential and respiratory capacity to levels comparable to attached cells, demonstrating that detachment-induced mitochondrial dysfunction is reversible upon reattachment. These findings align with previous work showing that anchorage-independent and clustered cancer cells undergo reversible metabolic reprogramming, including suppression of oxidative metabolism, engagement of reductive pathways to support redox homeostasis, and altered ROS handling to facilitate metastatic colonization. Collectively, this dissociation-based Seahorse workflow provides a practical and accessible platform to interrogate metabolic adaptations to anchorage-independent growth and cell clustering and identify bioenergetic vulnerabilities of metastasis-relevant cancer cell states. Key features • Dissociation-based Seahorse XF Mito Stress Test enabling per-cell bioenergetic profiling of anchorage-independent cancer cell clusters grown in ultra-low adherent plates. • Overcomes structural heterogeneity by enzymatically dissociating clusters into single-cell suspensions immediately before analysis, ensuring each viable cell contributes equally to OCR measurements. • Compatible with adherent monolayer, anchorage-independent, and reattached cell populations, enabling direct bioenergetic comparison across conditions that model primary tumor, circulating, and metastatic colonization states. • Validated in the A549 lung adenocarcinoma cell line; includes PDL coating, in-house DMEM preparation, and BAM15 concentration optimization steps adaptable to other cancer cell lines.

items.title: The impact and cost of reaching the UNAIDS global HIV targets.
items.authors: Stover J, Mattur D, Siapka M, Pliakas T, Valladares-Cardona R.
items.abstract: HIV funding has been declining in the past decade creating a large gap in required funding. In 2024, UNAIDS (Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS) convened a Global Task Team in 2024 to recommend new targets and approaches for 2030 for key HIV interventions. This paper describes the approach to estimate the impact and cost of achieving those targets. We calibrated an HIV simulation model, Goals, to the historical HIV epidemic in 134 countries and used the model to project the impact of achieving the UNAIDS targets by 2030. Resource needs were estimated for 118 low-, lower-middle and upper-middle income countries (LMIC). To estimate the cost of achieving the targets we compiled a database of the unit costs for each intervention from published studies, country reports and commodity costs. Achieving the UNAIDS 2030 targets would reduce the annual number of new HIV infections globally by 77% from 2023 to 2030, from 1.3 million to 300,000. The number of AIDS deaths would decline by 50% over the same period. Resources needed to achieve the targets in all LMIC would rise to US$21.9 billion by 2030. Of this amount, 17% is needed in low-income countries, 38% in lower-middle income countries and 45% in upper-middle income countries. Achieving the UNAIDS targets for 2030 would reduce the annual number of new HIV infections to just 9% of the peak value in 1995 and AIDS deaths to 13% of the peak value in 2004. The resources required to achieve these targets are substantial but $7 billion less than previous estimates of $29.3 billion.

items.title: Making long-acting HIV PrEP routine in college health: durable systems, not dedicated heroes.
items.authors: Broker P.
items.abstract: For many U.S. students, college health is the practical home of primary care and their most direct point of access to HIV prevention. In this commentary I argue that HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), including long-acting cabotegravir and lenacapavir, should be offered as routine preventive care in college health rather than as a specialty service. Nearly all responding student health services in national benchmarking data offer STI and HIV testing and contraception, while far fewer offer PrEP or prompt clinicians to educate patients on PrEP. That gap, the June 2025 approval of lenacapavir, and a quality improvement initiative that raised PrEP counseling from 3.0% to 97% point to a capacity-based framework of on-site, hybrid, and closed-loop referral models. The minimum standard is not identical infrastructure but a reliable pathway from routine offer to receipt of the chosen regimen. Clinics need durable systems rather than dedicated heroes.

items.title: Understanding community questions about HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP): A thematic analysis of reddit threads to inform development of an AI chatbot for PrEP education.
items.authors: Vincent-Paulraj A, Wood W, Marzolini C, Chiong J, Hodge D, Gibbons S, Seddon D, Martin J, Khoo S, Waker LE.
items.abstract:
Background

Despite growing availability of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), many potential users turn to online forums for advice and information collection. These forums provide a window into real-world questions, concerns and misinformation. They serve as a tool for users to query for sensitive information without revealing their identities. These platforms could therefore be a potential source of understanding of the unmet needs of users. This study systematically analyses the social media posts referring to the four drugs mentioned in the study to identify common questions and thematic concerns among the community and uses this insight to inform the design of an AI-driven, privacy-preserving chatbot for PrEP education based on evidence.

Methods

Between May 2011 to October 2025, we found 1168 relevant Reddit posts mentioning one of the four names for PrEP therapies, by either brand or generic name: Truvada (Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate + emtricitabine (TDF/FTC)), Descovy (Tenofovir alafenamide + emtricitabine (TAF/FTC)), Apretude (long-acting cabotegravir), Yeztugo (lenacapavir) using a systematic search. We used Natural Language processing (NLP) techniques to understand user needs.

Results

Seven distinct discussion themes were identified within PrEP social media discourse, with side effects emerging as the most frequently discussed primary topic among 1076 posts. Across all medications, weight changes were the most frequently mentioned side effect. Truvada was the most frequently discussed PrEP medication. 96.7% of the dataset comprised questions, showing that Reddit serves as a primary information-seeking platform. Early period discussions were emphasized basic access and effectiveness questions, with more recent discussions (2022-2025) displaying increased attention to injectable and long-term safety considerations.

Conclusions

Reddit users demonstrate persistent uncertainty about PrEP side effects, drug interactions and medication switching. Drug interactions represented the most frequently identified information gap (26.5% of posts). These empirically derived information needs will inform the design of a privacy-preserving PrEP chatbot trained on authoritative UK sources (hiv-druginteractions.org, BHIVA guidelines, NHS resources).

items.title: HIV-1 diagnosis during pre-exposure prophylaxis: A case report.
items.authors: Cruces L, Baquero L, Barletta JAE, Turk G, Laufer N.
items.abstract: We report a case of HIV diagnosis in a 36-year-old man who has sex with men receiving daily oral PrEP (emtricitabine/tenofovir) in Argentina, where viral load or HIV PCR testing is not routinely available before or during prophylaxis. In 2022, PrEP was initiated after a diagnosis of primary syphilis, with a non-reactive fourth-generation HIV test performed 13 days earlier (outside the recommended window), so very early infection already present at initiation cannot be excluded. Self-reported adherence was >95%. Serology was negative at day 23 and became reactive at day 73, with an indeterminate Western blot (gp120 only), undetectable plasma HIV-RNA and preserved lymphocyte counts; dolutegravir was added to complete antiretroviral treatment. Standard diagnostic algorithms were initially inconclusive, and confirmation required approaches beyond routine practice: HIV-1 RNA was detected only after ultracentrifugation of 14 mL of plasma (55 copies), and low-level proviral HIV-1 DNA was identified after analysis of an extensive number of cells; Nef- and p24-specific T-cell responses were also detected. No resistance-associated mutations were found on proviral DNA (integrase region). The Western blot eventually became positive at day 382, while a rapid immunochromatographic assay remained negative at 34 months. Atypical presentations of this kind have been reported under oral TDF/FTC PrEP and were subsequently characterized as long-acting early viral inhibition (LEVI) syndrome, predominantly in the context of long-acting cabotegravir. The present case illustrates the extent of non-routine investigation required to confirm HIV acquisition, and the challenges this poses in settings where oral PrEP is the only available option and HIV-1 RNA PCR cannot be routinely deployed. PrEP should be initiated promptly following a negative HIV test performed on the same day, or as close as possible to PrEP initiation, particularly when recent exposure is possible. HIV testing should be repeated sequentially after initiation, and discordant results should prompt continued serological and molecular evaluation.

items.title: Immune Imprinting Across Respiratory Virus Infection, Vaccination, and Passive Immunization: Rethinking 'Original Antigenic Sin' in Influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV.
items.authors: Szuster-Ciesielska A.
items.abstract: Immune imprinting shapes every subsequent response to antigenically related pathogens and is now central to designing updated vaccines for influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The label "Original Antigenic Sin" has framed imprinting as a fixed liability, but recent germinal-center, B-cell repertoire, and epidemiological data show that the effect is neither uniformly harmful nor irreversible. This review distinguishes cross-reactive immune memory from immune imprinting, defined here as a preferential bias toward the first-encountered antigen. Prior exposure can provide useful cross-reactive memory, but available evidence generally does not show that first-antigen bias itself improves protection relative to an equivalent unbiased memory response. We therefore use a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework to examine how antigenic distance, conserved-epitope accessibility, and exposure interval may influence both the usefulness of recalled memory and the extent to which imprinting restricts recruitment of responses to later antigens. The framework organizes existing observations and is not intended to predict imprinting outcomes ex ante. We discuss recent quantitative models that explicitly formalize competition between memory and de novo responses as complementary, pathogen-specific approaches. Across influenza and SARS-CoV-2, early exposure can establish cross-reactive memory associated with subsequent heterologous protection, while preferential recall of the priming antigen may limit responses to novel epitopes. For RSV, the effects of maternal vaccination and passive antibodies on subsequent active immune memory remain uncertain. Immunogen engineering, schedule adjustment, adjuvant selection, and cohort-tailored strategies may broaden pre-existing memory toward conserved protective epitopes and reduce restrictive first-antigen bias.

items.title: Microneedle-mediated co-delivery of biomimetic melanin and pro-regenerative factors for oxidative and immune modulation in vitiligo.
items.authors: Liang J, Liu W, Jiang Y, Yu Y, Li Q, Zhang Y, Li W, Zhang X.
items.abstract: Vitiligo lesions are characterized by elevated epidermal oxidative stress, cytotoxic immune activation, and impaired melanogenesis, while conventional topical therapies often fail to modulate these pathogenic events due to limited skin penetration and therapeutic depth. To address these challenges, a dual-layer gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)/hyaluronic acid methacryloyl (HAMA)//hyaluronic acid (HA) (Gel//HA) microneedle system was engineered. The inner HA layer rapidly dissolves upon insertion, releasing keratinocyte-membrane-coated artificial melanin nanoparticles (MPDA) to achieve early reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging and targeted delivery to keratinocytes. The outer Gel hydrogel layer enables sustained intradermal delivery of basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) and tyrosinase (TYR), supporting melanocyte survival and restoring melanin synthesis. The microneedles exhibited robust mechanical strength (0.234 ± 0.014 N/needle) with a penetration depth of approximately 300-350 μm. In vitro, the cumulative release of bFGF and TYR reached 65% and 70% within the first 72 h, respectively, and subsequently increased more gradually to 92.1% and 90.7% by day 21. In vitro, the combined administration of MPDA, bFGF, and TYR, mitigated H2O2-induced oxidative injury and enhanced keratinocyte viability. In a monobenzone-induced mouse model, Gel@bFGF/TYR//HA@MPDA treatment markedly promoted repigmentation, restored epidermal melanin deposition, and reduced the expression of CD8, IFN-γ, and TNF-α. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed suppression of ferroptosis-related genes and reactivation of the Wnt-Frizzled-MITF melanogenic signaling axis. This spatially designed microneedle system provides coordinated antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and pro-melanogenic effects, offering a promising localized therapeutic strategy for vitiligo.

Veterinary drug residues in animal-derived foods: From analytical detection to intelligent and sustainable surveillance.
items.authors: Ramezani Farani M, Mirzaee D, Voosough A, Hatami A, Chanmey K, Miraei Ashtiani SH, Sheik A, Alipourfard I, Ch Stratakos A, A Piletsky S, Hwang SK, Huh YS.
items.abstract: Veterinary drug residues in animal-derived foods remain a major challenge for food safety, public health, and international trade. This review examines residue control through the complementary roles of analytical technologies, digital tools and green analytical chemistry. Rapid screening can support local decisions, while liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry provides laboratory confirmation. Digital tools offer opportunities to connect analytical results with treatment records and product traceability, but their value depends on data quality, interoperability and validation. Solvent reduction and miniaturization should be assessed alongside energy use and material life cycles. The proposed farm-to-fork roadmap links these approaches with regulatory requirements and One Health priorities, emphasizing reliable measurements, coordinated data use and feasibility in resource-constrained settings.

items.title: Trends in and program characteristics associated with pre-exposure prophylaxis availability among opioid treatment facilities in the United States.
items.authors: Figgatt MC, Jaiswal J, Alnashri Y, Rosen JG, Rich JD, Green TC.
items.abstract:
Objective

To examine the prevalence and settings of PrEP availability at opioid use treatment facilities in the United States.

Methods

We examined PrEP trends from 2021 to 2024 using the National Substance Use and Mental Health Services Survey. Using multivariable logistic regression models, we calculated odds ratios (OR) and their 95% confidence intervals (CI) to examine associations between facility characteristics and PrEP prescribing in 2024.

Results

A total of 13,755 substance use treatment facilities in 2021; 14,201 in 2022; 12,892 in 2023; and 13,875 in 2024 were included. The percentage of facilities offering PrEP increased from 6.03% in 2021 to 10.62% in 2024 (p < 0.01) nationwide. Despite comprising over 90% of facilities, outpatient (8.57%) and residential (14.26%) facilities had lower PrEP availability than inpatient facilities (23.19%). Facilities with methadone and buprenorphine had higher odds of PrEP availability (methadone OR = 7.52, 95% CI = 5.34, 10.59; buprenorphine only OR = 10.09, 95% CI = 7.53, 13.52) compared to those without these treatments. Facilities offering programs specific to people living with HIV (OR = 2.32, 95% CI = 1.83, 2.94) and those identifying as LGBTQ+ (OR = 1.75, 95% CI = 1.35, 2.27) were more likely to offer PrEP.

Conclusions

Despite the high number of people served in outpatient and residential facilities, PrEP access continues to remain low.

items.title: Nanomaterials Reshaping Tumor Metabolism: A New Frontier to Overcome T Cell Exhaustion.
items.authors: Zhu X, He L, Li J, Guo S, Liu X, Cao Y, Song S.
items.abstract: Adoptive antitumor immunity ultimately fails because metabolically hostile tumor microenvironments (TME) drive T cells into a dysfunctional exhausted state that current checkpoint blockade only partially reverses. Crucially, the principal metabolic stresses - accumulation of lactate, lipids and adenosine, deprivation of glucose and amino acids, and hypoxia - do not act in isolation but form a densely cross-regulated network that progressively reinforces T cell exhaustion. This review synthesizes how each barrier arises and how they amplify one another, then maps nanomaterial-based countermeasures onto this network: catalytic nanomaterials that degrade lactate and adenosine, lipid-modulating and mitochondria-targeted formulations, amino-acid replenishment systems, and hypoxia-relieving designs that pair metabolic correction with checkpoint inhibition or photodynamic therapy. Particular attention is given to the design principles - tissue targeting, stimuli-responsive release and rational combination - that determine whether metabolic reprogramming yields durable restoration of T cell function rather than transient phenotypic rescue. Emerging preclinical evidence indicates that nanomaterial-mediated metabolic remodeling can convert the immunosuppressive TME into an immune-supportive niche and recover effector function of exhausted T cells. We further identify the key gaps that currently limit clinical translation: the absence of subset-level evaluation distinguishing reversible progenitor-like exhausted T cells from terminally exhausted cells, the lack of epigenetic endpoints such as histone lactylation, off-target metabolic suppression of T cells themselves, and the manufacturing and safety hurdles of clinical-grade nanomaterials. Resolving these issues would establish metabolic reprogramming as a credible frontier for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Numerous linked cases of acute genotype F hepatitis B virus infections in people living with HIV or on pre-exposure prophylaxis.
items.authors: Rouget R, Leducq V, Maylin S, Gozlan J, Thibault V, Valantin MA, Mercier-Delarue S, Faycal A, Valin N, Wirden M, Cocherie T, Akhavan S, Roque-Afonso AM, Sayon S, Chevaliez S, Bouille T, Fauchois A, Calvez V, Marcelin AG, Lacombe K, Delaugerre C, Pourcher V, Manda V, Seang S, Todesco E.
items.abstract:
Objectives

At least 2.7 million people living with HIV are infected with hepatitis B virus (HBV) worldwide. Some antiretroviral treatments and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-based pre-exposure prophylaxis protect against HBV infection. However, emerging antiretroviral strategies without any activity against HBV may promote spread of this virus in the future. In this context, we studied recent cases of acute HBV infection in people at risk of sexually transmitted infections. Our objective was to better understand HBV circulation and the dynamics of its transmission.

Methods

This retrospective study included people diagnosed with acute HBV infections between 2022 and 2025 in France. The whole HBV genome was amplified and sequenced by next-generation sequencing for network analysis.

Results

Sixteen men, with a median age of 35 years, were enrolled. Six were living with HIV, including three receiving long-acting injectable cabotegravir/rilpivirine treatment. Four of the HIV-negative individuals were taking pre-exposure prophylaxis. Nine had been vaccinated against HBV, and six had anti-HBs antibody titres between 10 and 100 IU/L. Analysis revealed HBV genotype F1b in 14 patients, with very high homology among the viruses. No known immune escape mutations were identified, even in the individuals with anti-HBs antibodies.

Conclusions

A transmission cluster of HBV F1b genotype was observed in a population at risk of infection. This genotype, which is endemic to Latin America, is rarely detected in France. These findings may serve as a timely reminder of the ongoing circulation of HBV among exposed populations. HBV transmission among vaccinated individuals with positive anti-HBs antibodies raises questions and should be further studied.

items.title: Development and implementation of a pharmacy PrEP awareness-raising and referral pathway: acceptability and feasibility of a UK pilot.
items.authors: Harrison C, Harryman L, Stockwell S, Family H, Kesten JM, Denford S, Scott J, Sabin C, Copping J, Saunders J, Hamilton-Shaw R, Symonds N, Dick OB, Tarmey E, Horwood J.

items.title: A scoping review of pre-exposure prophylaxis awareness, acceptability, uptake, adherence, and HIV-related risk behaviors among university students in South Africa.
items.authors: Serebane MJ, Ramavhoya TI, Mutshatshi TE, Mokhwelepa LW.
items.abstract:
Background

Pre-exposure prophylaxis is an effective biomedical intervention for preventing HIV infection, yet evidence on its awareness, acceptability, uptake and adherence among South African university students remains fragmented.

Objective

To map and synthesize the available evidence on pre-exposure prophylaxis awareness, acceptability, uptake, adherence, and HIV-related risk behaviors among university students in South Africa.

Methods

A scoping review was conducted using Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported according to PRISMA-ScR. Studies published between 2014 and 2026 were searched in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, CINAHL, African Journals Online and ProQuest Dissertations and Theses/grey literature. Two reviewers independently screened studies and charted data using a predefined extraction tool. Findings were synthesized thematically.

Results

Sixteen studies were included, of which 68.75% (n = 11) were quantitative and 31.25% (n = 5) qualitative. Evidence was concentrated in KwaZulu-Natal, Gauteng, Limpopo and the Western Cape, with most studies published from 2019 onwards. Six themes emerged: (1) Individual Level: individual perceptions, knowledge and appraisal of HIV and PrEP; (2) Interpersonal Level: interpersonal relationships and social influence on PrEP decision-making; (3) Institutional Level: accessibility, acceptability and responsiveness of PrEP services; (4) Community/social Level: stigma, misconceptions and social norms surrounding PrEP; (5) Structural Level: socioeconomic and health-system conditions shaping PrEP utilization; and (6) HIV Risk Behaviors: patterns of sexual risk and their relationship to PrEP need. Awareness and willingness to use PrEP were generally favorable, but uptake and sustained use were constrained by knowledge gaps, low perceived risk, stigma, side-effect concerns, cost, accessibility and service-related barriers. Risk behaviors included multiple partnerships, inconsistent condom use, substance-associated sexual behavior and socioeconomic pressures.

Conclusion

PrEP utilization is shaped by interacting individual, social, institutional and structural factors. Integrated, youth-friendly services and targeted education addressing HIV risk, stigma and access are needed to strengthen informed PrEP decision-making and prevention.

items.title: HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis in US prison settings: a model-based cost-effectiveness study.
items.authors: Park Y, Goldhaber-Fiebert JD, Cipriano LE.
items.abstract:
Background

HIV prevalence in prisons is three times higher than in the general community, and ongoing transmission risks highlight the importance of prevention, including pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). We evaluated the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of prison-based PrEP programs in four US states.

Methods

We developed a dynamic compartmental model simulating HIV transmission in both general and incarcerated populations, instantiated for four representative US states (standardized population of five million people). We assessed five strategies involving PrEP for specific risk groups in prison compared to the status quo of no PrEP. We assumed 25% uptake among eligible individuals for 20 years. We estimated total lifetime costs (in 2024 USD) and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), discounted at 3% annually, incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), and HIV infections averted from a healthcare sector perspective.

Findings

In Washington, New York, and Georgia, providing PrEP to 25% of people who inject drugs (PWID) in prison prevented 12%-14% of new infections in incarcerated people, and 0.01%-0.02% of new infections in the community, and was cost-saving compared to no PrEP. Expanding eligibility to all high-risk persons (PWID and men who have sex with men (MSM)) prevented more infections and cost less than $60,000 per QALY gained compared to more restrictive policies. In California, where the epidemic is concentrated among MSM rather than PWID, providing PrEP to only MSM costs $32,000 per QALY gained.

Interpretation

Prison-based PrEP programs can be cost-saving or cost-effective, averting infections within and outside the prison system. These findings support expanding access to PrEP in prisons, with implementation and funding decisions guided by local HIV epidemiology.
